{{Quote|I am the Dark Lord who will restore the Sith to glory. They call me Bane.|Darth Bane|<ref Name="JvS 6">[[Jedi vs. Sith 6|''Jedi vs. Sith'' 6]]</ref>}}
'''Darth Bane''', [[Reproduction/Legends|born]] '''Dessel''', and known to his proxies as '''Lord Eddels''', was the [[Sith'ari/Legends|Sith'ari]] and the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] responsible for creating the [[Rule of Two/Legends|Rule of Two]]. Born in [[1026 BBY]], he was raised as a poor [[Mining/Legends|miner]] on the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Apatros/Legends|Apatros]]. After [[Death/Legends|killing]] a [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] [[Ensign/Legends|ensign]] when the soldier tried to mug him in [[1003 BBY]], Dessel was in danger of being arrested and [[Prison/Legends|imprisoned]] by the Republic. With the help of his friend [[Groshik]], he escaped off-world to join the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Brotherhood of Darkness/Legends|Brotherhood of Darkness]]. Initially serving as a foot [[Soldier/Legends|soldier]] in the [[Gloom Walkers]] unit, he was recognized as a [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]], and taken to the [[Sith Academy (Korriban)|Sith Academy]] on [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]]. Bane, as he had been baptised, quickly became one of the best students at the Academy before he lost his faith in the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]]. Though Bane was able to regain his confidence in the dark side, he lost his trust in the Brotherhood of Darkness, believing it to be a flawed organization whose leader, [[Skere Kaan]], was a coward and a fool. Deserting the order, he went to the planet Lehon and studied the [[Darth Revan's Sith Holocron|holocron]] of [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] [[Revan/Legends|Revan]], and, armed with new knowledge, helped him deceive and destroy the Brotherhood using a [[thought bomb]] which targeted all force sensitives including the remaining [[Army of Light]] Jedi lead by Lord Hoth on [[Seventh Battle of Ruusan|Ruusan]], leading to the [[Ruusan Reformations/Legends|Ruusan reformations]] and the alleged destruction of the Sith, allowing him to create his own [[Order of the Sith Lords|Sith Order]]. Hiding from the Jedi Order, he then instituted a Rule of Two, which stated that there could be only two Sith to avoid the infighting that had plagued the Sith for millennia. He also took both the title of [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] and an [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]] named [[Darth Zannah/Legends|Darth Zannah]].

In [[990 BBY]], [[1000 BBY/Legends|ten years after the destruction of the Brotherhood]], Bane sought to learn how to create a [[Holocron/Legends|holocron]], through which he would pass down his knowledge to future [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lords]]. The Sith [[Mission to Tython|journeyed]] to the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]] world of [[Tython/Legends|Tython]] to locate the [[Sith holocron/Legends|Sith holocron]] of the ancient Dark Lord [[Belia Darzu]]. However, while Bane was on Tython, the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] learned of his existence, and sent a group of [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] to kill him and his apprentice. Once the Jedi arrived, they [[Duel on Tython|confronted]] the two Sith in Darzu's fortress. Though outnumbered, the Sith were able to defeat the Jedi; however, Bane was grievously injured. Zannah took him to [[Ambria/Legends|Ambria]], where she convinced the healer [[Caleb]] to help them. Caleb notified the [[Jedi Council/Legends|Jedi Council]], only to have Zannah use her [[Sith sorcery/Legends|powers]] to [[Summon fear|drive]] her cousin [[Darovit]] insane. Zannah killed Caleb, then [[Spell of concealment|hid herself and Bane]]. When the Jedi arrived, they were attacked by and [[Confrontation on Ambria|killed]] Darovit, believing him to be the Sith Lord. Thus, the Sith were believed destroyed.

[[980 BBY|A decade later]], Bane began to worry that his apprentice was too weak to overthrow him and assume the mantle of Dark Lord of the Sith, as was necessary under the Rule of Two. He began to research the secrets to prolonging his life by [[Essence transfer|transferring his essence]] to another body, and traveled to [[Prakith/Legends|Prakith]], where he [[Mission to Prakith (Darth Bane)|claimed]] the [[Holocron of Heresies|holocron]] of the ancient [[Darth Andeddu]]. After returning from Prakith, Bane was [[Skirmish in Darth Bane's mansion|ambushed]] by a team of [[Assassin/Legends|assassins]] hired by Caleb's daughter, [[Serra]], and was captured. Taken to [[Doan]], Bane was imprisoned and tortured, only to covertly gain his freedom soon afterward. Encountering Zannah on Doan, Bane [[Duel on Doan|dueled]] his apprentice, who sought to become the new Dark Lord. The fight ended in a draw, with Bane escaping and heading to Ambria with [[Darth Cognus]], an [[Iktotchi/Legends|Iktotchi]] assassin skilled in use of the dark side whom Bane planned to take as his apprentice if Zannah proved herself weak and unworthy. There, Bane and Zannah engaged in a [[Duel on Ambria (980 BBY)|fateful duel]] that resulted in the death of the Sith'ari and Zannah claiming the title of Dark Lord. Bane tried to initiate the ritual of essence transfer but failed to control his apprentice's body. Part of Darth Bane's soul lived in Zannah's body after the failed ritual. But the majority of his spirit was thrown into the void, causing him an eternity of suffering. Nearly a [[19 BBY/Legends|millennium later]], Bane's Sith Order [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|defeated]] the Jedi Order and [[Declaration of a New Order|overthrew]] the Republic. His holocron still imparted wisdom through the years.

==Biography==
===Early life===
{{Quote|Hurst always said you were no good. He knew there was something wrong with you&hellip;Bane.|Gerd|<ref name="pod" />}}
[[File:NewSithWars.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Dessel grew up as a cortosis miner and was far removed from the New Sith Wars (pictured).]]
The [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] who would become [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Bane was [[Reproduction/Legends|born]] as Dessel on the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Apatros/Legends|Apatros]] to an abusive [[Mining/Legends|miner]] named [[Hurst]]. Des, as he was nicknamed, was often bullied by his father and the other miners. Hurst blamed his son for the [[Death/Legends|death]] of his [[Marriage/Legends|wife]], who had perished during childbirth. Hurst also took to blaming Dessel for his own miserable life on Apatros, and considered his son to be the bane of his existence&mdash;so much so that he took to calling him "bane" frequently. At the age of sixteen, Dessel began to work in the [[Cortosis/Legends|cortosis]] mines of Apatros under the direction of the [[Outer Rim Oreworks Company]]. He learned to fend for himself, ignoring the threats and insults hurled at him by his father and the other miners, and grew into a muscular young man as he worked deep in the cortosis mines. One of Dessel's few friends was [[Groshik]], the [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidian]] owner of the [[Groshik's cantina|local cantina]]. Unknown to anyone, Dessel was [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]], and he occasionally felt the call of [[The Force/Legends|the Force's]] [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]].<ref name="pod" />

One [[Standard day/Legends|day]], when Dessel was eighteen, a drunk Hurst berated him until Dessel stood up to his father and challenged him to a fight. Irate, Hurst beat him until his ribs cracked, although Dessel withstood the pain without sound. That night, Dessel, filled with hate, envisioned his father dying by picturing a giant hand squeezing his [[Heart/Legends|heart]]. The next morning, Hurst was dead. Unknown to Dessel, he had used the Force to kill his father. After Hurst's death, his friends tried to continue with their harassment of Dessel, but the young miner now had the confidence to stand up for himself, and proceeded to best many of them in fights until they learned to leave him alone. On the fifth anniversary of Hurst's death, a man named [[Gerd]]&mdash;who had been friends with Hurst&mdash;decided that he would put Dessel in his place after verbally harassing him the same way Hurst once did. In a drunken stupor, Gerd attacked Dessel and attempted to gouge out one of his eyes. With a premonition granted by the dark side of the Force, Dessel severed Gerd's thumb with his [[Tooth/Legends|teeth]].<ref name="pod" />

Returning to town on a [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] cargo [[Starship/Legends|ship]], Dessel began playing [[Sabacc/Legends|sabacc]] in [[Groshik's cantina]] against other miners and a group of Republic [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]] who had arrived to pick up cortosis shipments from Outer Rim Oreworks. A skilled [[Gambling/Legends|gambler]], Dessel proceeded to win many games while also tossing frequent barbs at the Republic to the soldiers in the [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]]. Successfully driving every other player out of the game, Dessel played his final hand against a young [[Ensign/Legends|ensign]], and both ended up with an [[Idiot's Array/Legends|Idiot's Array]], the rarest hand possible. In a [[Sudden demise|final round]] where whoever was dealt the highest card would win, both players received nine. In the next sudden death round, Dessel got a nine, beating the ensign's eight, and giving him sabacc and the ten thousand [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credit]] sabacc pot. The irate ensign attempted to attack Dessel, but was stopped by [[Groshik]]. Groshik also ordered everyone but Dessel out, and explained to the Human that he was worried; Dessel had somehow played the soldiers, twisting them to his advantage and never relenting. Furthermore, the crowd had somehow fed off of Dessel's anger, Groshik believed. Dessel reassured his friend, but the [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidian]] warned him to be careful.<ref name="pod" />

As Dessel left the cantina, he was attacked by the ensign and two other soldiers. Easily dominated by the miner in physical combat, the ensign pulled out a [[Vibroblade/Legends|vibroblade]]. However, Dessel's unconscious use of the Force allowed him to detect the weapon. Reacting without thinking, Dessel stabbed the ensign with his own weapon, killing the soldier. Panicked, the other Republic soldiers fled to alert their superiors. The miner was forced to turn to Groshik, who used his contacts to save Dessel from being caught and imprisoned by Republic forces by arranging to have him smuggled off-planet to join the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]]&mdash;the enemies of the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] and the Republic, who engaged in a prolonged [[New Sith Wars|war]] with them.<ref name="pod" />

===New Sith Wars===
{{Quote|Now you get to see firsthand how the Brotherhood of Darkness deals with mutinous soldiers!|Ulabore|<ref name="pod" />}}
[[File:Gloom_Walkers.png|thumb|left|300px|Dessel among the Gloom Walkers]]
Dessel was hidden onboard a [[Rodian/Legends|Rodian's]] starship, and taken to join the [[Brotherhood of Darkness/Legends|Brotherhood of Darkness]] as a foot soldier, helping to win the New Sith Wars. The Human quickly rose to the rank of [[Sergeant/Legends|sergeant]] in a Sith unit known as the [[Gloom Walkers]]. Wielding a [[GSI-21D]] and a [[TC-22 blaster rifle|TC-22]], he became a skilled shot. His use of the Force made him an adept soldier and [[Commander/Legends|commander]], and he was able to guide his unit away from death many times, such as during the [[Battle of Kashyyyk (New Sith Wars)|Battle of Kashyyyk]]. For his actions, Dessel earned the trust of the Gloom Walkers over that of the unit's commander, [[Ulabore]], who took credit for his unit's victories, which had been enabled by Dessel. The Gloom Walkers soon became one of the most skilled of the Sith's infantry units, and they were sent on the most critical missions.<ref name="pod" />

However, things changed for Dessel after the Gloom Walkers received an order regarding the [[Battle of Phaseera]]. Ulabore knew the order to be a tactical mistake but planned to follow it anyway since he was afraid to face the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] who had issued the command. Dessel mutinied and punched Ulabore in the face, knocking him out cold, and then proceeded to lead the squad into battle. After being blinded by a [[Flash grenade/Legends|flash grenade]], Dessel discovered that he could still "see" where all the Republic soldiers were. Thanks to this mysterious sight, he managed to kill each soldier with a [[Sniper/Legends|sniper]] rifle in the space of a few seconds. Though he did not know it at the time, he had unconsciously used the Force. After the battle, Dessel discovered that Ulabore had informed the Sith Lord [[Kopecz]] of his actions. Expecting to be court-martialed, Dessel was saved from this fate by the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord]], who offered to take him to [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]] where he could enroll at the [[Sith Academy (Korriban)|Sith Academy]]. Dessel decided to accept Kopecz's offer. Having been offered the chance to create a new identity for himself, he thought back to the cruelty of his father, and decided to take a new name, one which would signify his new life&mdash;Bane.<ref name="pod" />

===Training on Korriban===
{{Quote|I think he might be the one we've been searching for. He could be the Sith'ari.|Kopecz|<ref name="pod" />}}
Bane arrived at the Academy and immediately began to study the ways of the Sith under the Sith Lords [[Qordis]] and [[Kas'im]]. On his own initiative, he also frequently studied the archives in the academy, which contained documents about the dark side and the history of the Sith. However, the [[Sith Master/Legends|Sith Masters]] discouraged the studying of the archives, claiming they were relics of a time long forgotten. Thanks in part to the Masters' advice, Bane began to abandon the archives he studied at the beginning of his training in favor of increased focus on physical and mental exercise. Despite the late discovery of his Force-sensitivity, Bane began to exceed many of the students who had been [[Sith training|trained]] since birth.<ref name="pod" />

[[File:DarthBane.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Darth Bane]]

After training for several [[Standard month/Legends|months]] and rapidly climbing to the top of the ranks among the students, Bane challenged to a duel a [[Makurth/Legends|Makurth]] student named [[Fohargh]] who had previously beaten him. After beating Bane in [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|combat]], Fohargh began to taunt him, causing Bane to fill with rage. He unleashed his anger, killing Fohargh with a wave of dark Force energy against Kas'im's instructions. This victory earned Bane the attention of the [[Zabrak/Legends|Zabrak]] [[Sirak]], the favorite of Lord Qordis and one of the most prominent students at the academy. Though Bane expected to be punished for killing a fellow student, Qordis instead was impressed by Bane, and began urging the [[Sith Blademaster|Blademaster]] Kas'im to pay special attention to Bane.<ref name="pod" />

However, the victory left Bane shaken. The [[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentice]] realized that he had been responsible for the death of his father [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before. This revelation caused Bane to doubt the Masters' teachings, and he began to fear the power of the dark side. As a result, he also started to lose his connection to it. Realizing that unless he acted quickly he would fall behind the other students, he challenged Sirak. The Zabrak easily bested Bane, nearly killing him. After his loss, Bane was shunned by the other Sith, including his former mentors. Becoming somewhat of an outcast, he desperately turned to the archives once more. From them, he learned more about the history of the Sith and the power of the dark side. Bane began to question the direction the Brotherhood of Darkness had taken, and he seemed especially interested in finding out why none of the current Sith Lords took the title [[Darth/Legends|Darth]]. He began to believe that the Brotherhood was inherently flawed, and ruled by pretenders. Upon questioning Kas'im later, Bane learned that the leader of the Brotherhood, [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] [[Skere Kaan]] had forbidden any Sith from taking the title Darth, as he claimed that the use of this title would only encourage the infighting that had nearly destroyed the Sith thousands of years earlier.<ref name="pod" />

During this time, a Jedi deserter named [[Githany]] arrived, and Bane saw his chance to reclaim his place among the other students. Githany in turn saw Bane as a tool she could use against Sirak, her only real rival at the Academy. Requesting that Githany secretly teach him Force techniques she learned from the masters, Bane also began private [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|lightsaber combat]] instruction with Kas'im. Neither teacher was aware of the other, ensuring that Bane had an edge over both. Bane and Githany soon began to realize that they had feelings for each other, though neither wanted to admit it. As his training progressed, Bane learned far more from the archives at the Academy than he had originally thought possible, and continued supplementing his knowledge of the Force with the teachings of the ancient Sith. Bane mastered many [[Force power/Legends|Force powers]] while perfecting his lightsaber techniques.<ref name="pod" />

When he believed himself to be ready, Bane once again challenged Sirak to a duel. The Human played his opponent, wearing him down before wounding him, sending a humiliated Sirak to the medical wing. Following this victory, Kas'im presented Bane with a [[Curved-hilt lightsaber/Legends|curved-hilt lightsaber]] that had previously belonged to his own master, a Sith Lord named [[Na'daz]], who had saved the Blademaster from [[Slavery/Legends|slavery]] on [[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]]. Kas'im also revealed that he had killed his master in a personal test of skill and took his weapon as a reminder of what his master taught him. This revelation left a lasting impression on Bane.<ref name="pod" />

Once again under the gaze of the Academy Masters, Bane was summoned by Qordis, who revealed to the apprentice that he had been aware for some time that Githany was teaching him. Qordis then told Bane that he was to stop studying the archives. Bane, whose doubts about the Brotherhood had only grown, was angered, and defied Qordis by leaving the Academy for the [[Valley of the Dark Lords/Legends|Valley of the Dark Lords]] in search of answers from the tombs of long-dead Sith Lords. However, Bane found no [[Force ghost/Legends|Sith spirits]] in the tombs, concluding that they judged the current Sith to be weak and unworthy. Bane believed that the Brotherhood was flawed, and that Kaan placed the greater good of the order over the dark side as a whole, preventing the Sith from defeating the Jedi Order.<ref name="pod" />

Nearly dead from exhaustion and hunger, Bane returned to the Academy two weeks later to learn that the students were to be raised to the level of Dark Lords of the Sith on the orders of Lord Kaan, and were to be sent to the planet [[Ruusan/Legends|Ruusan]] to participate in battle against the Jedi [[Army of Light/Legends|Army of Light]]. Bane was greeted by Githany, who informed him of the news, and led him to the archives. Unknown to Bane, she had secretly entered into an allegiance with Sirak, who wished to kill him. In the archives, Bane was attacked by Sirak and his allies [[Llokay]] and [[Yevra]]. However, Githany then betrayed Sirak by giving Bane his lightsaber and entering the fight on his side. She killed Llokay and Yevra while Bane disarmed his rival. Sirak begged for mercy, claiming that if Bane spared him, the Zabrak would serve him. Ignoring his pleas, Bane [[Sai cha/Legends|decapitated]] Sirak, releasing all his fears and guilt in the process and fully opening himself to the dark side.<ref name="pod" />

As Githany proclaimed that the two were now Dark Lords bound for Ruusan, Bane explained to her that he planned to go elsewhere. He denounced Kaan's Brotherhood, even when Githany praised Kaan and begged him to wait. Marching to Qordis's chamber, Bane confronted the Sith Lord, asking if he had ordered Sirak to kill him. Qordis was horrified that Bane had killed one of the Academy's most skilled students. However, Bane ignored his anger, denouncing Qordis and the other masters as cowards. Taking the title of Darth, Bane proclaimed that he was leaving the Brotherhood. The Human headed for the rooftop, where Qordis's personal starship, the ''[[Valcyn/Legends|Valcyn]]'', was docked. Boarding it, Bane set a course for the planet [[Lehon/Legends|Lehon]] in the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]], hoping to find true understanding of the dark side.<ref name="pod" />

===Lehon and the Holocron of Darth Revan===
{{Quote|The dark side is strong here. Far stronger than it ever was on Korriban. This is where we will find the power to destroy the Jedi&mdash;not in Kaan's Brotherhood!|Bane|<ref name="pod" />}}
[[File:Bane_headshot_Legends.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Darth Bane, architect of the Rule of Two]]
After landing on Lehon, Bane began his search for the [[Temple of the Ancients]], and along the way managed to tame a wild [[Rancor/Legends|rancor]] to be used as his steed. He felt a much stronger connection to the dark side on Lehon than he did on Korriban, which further reinforced his belief that the Brotherhood's decisions were flawed. Once he made his way to the temple, Bane began searching for any dark side relics. Though the temple appeared empty, he sensed a great power hidden there, and so continued to search until he located a [[Darth Revan's Sith Holocron|holocron]] that had been created by the Sith Lord [[Revan/Legends|Darth Revan]] millennia ago. Thrilled at having his faith rewarded, Bane activated the [[Holocron/Legends|holocron]], and spent several weeks studying it. From the holocron, Bane learned a tremendous deal about the dark side and Sith&mdash;more than he had learned in his entire time at the academy, he felt. The knowledge he gained from this holocron validated his view that the Brotherhood needed to be destroyed for the Sith to conquer the Jedi.<ref name="pod" />

Meanwhile, Kaan, fearful of Bane and his intentions, dispatched Kas'im from Ruusan to kill his former student. Thanks to Githany, who had had a [[Force vision/Legends|vision]] of Bane on Lehon, Kaan knew where to send the Blademaster. The [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] Master made his way to the planet, and then confronted Bane in the temple, revealing that he intended to kill him. After a [[Duel on Lehon|heated lightsaber duel]], Bane gained the upper hand, and forced Kas'im into a corner. However, the Blademaster split his [[Double-bladed lightsaber/Legends|double-bladed lightsaber]], wielding it as [[Interlocking hilt|two separate blades]]. During training Kas'im had always derided [[Jar'Kai/Legends|fighting with two lightsabers]], ensuring Bane had no experience facing such an opponent. Where Bane had been sure of victory only just moments before, his inexperience put him at a severe disadvantage, and he quickly lost his momentum. Bane was sent tumbling down a staircase as Kas'im advanced, ready to deliver the killing blow. Furious at himself and Kas'im, Bane remembered that he knew the layout of the temple, an advantage the Blademaster lacked. He unleashed his anger into a blast of dark Force energy, and though Kas'im managed to throw up a Force shield to protect himself, the blast caused the temple to collapse on the Twi'lek, killing him.<ref name="pod" /> Bane then dispatched a [[Message drone|messenger drone]] to Ruusan, informing Kaan of Kas'im's death and handing the Sith Lord instructions to perform the Sith ritual to make a [[thought bomb]], one of the many secrets he had learned from Revan's holocron. The Dark Lord kept this secret from the other Sith.<ref name="pod" /><ref name="Contradiction">There is a contradiction here between canonical sources. See the [[#Behind the scenes|''Behind the scenes'']] section for more details.</ref>

===Near-death on Ambria===
{{Quote|I am Darth Bane, Dark Lord of the Sith. I will survive. At any cost.|Bane|<ref name="pod" />}}
[[File:Bane_15.jpg|thumb|right|180px|Darth Bane on Ambria]]
By then, Kaan believed that a military victory on Ruusan was certain. An [[Orbit/Legends|orbital]] [[Blockade/Legends|blockade]] sustained by the Sith battle armada kept Jedi [[Farfalla's Knights|reinforcements]] from landing on the planet. Not long after sending Kas'im after Bane, Kaan received a message from the disillusioned Sith, who stated that he wished to return to the Brotherhood. However, Githany believed that the Brotherhood no longer needed Bane and offered to kill him. Believing Bane to be a threat, Kaan agreed and she left to meet with her former love interest.<ref name="pod" />

Bane chose the barren world [[Ambria/Legends|Ambria]] to meet Kaan's envoy. [[Lake Natth]], a body of black and poisonous [[Water/Legends|water]], had become the focus for the dark side energy on the planet, and Bane made his camp on its shores. While Bane waited for Githany he considered a question he still could not answer; once he had eliminated the Brotherhood, where would he find an apprentice worthy of the knowledge he had to impart? When Githany arrived they shared a passionate kiss, but Bane tasted [[Poison/Legends|poison]] on her lips and realized that Kaan had sent her to Ambria to kill him, although he kept this realization secret, believing that the small amount of poison was not enough to subdue him. Seeing that Githany understood the source of the strength in the dark side, Bane wondered if she could become his apprentice. He realized, though, that she believed too strongly in Kaan and the Brotherhood to accept his knowledge, and he sent her away, confident that her poison would have no effect on him.<ref name="pod" />

After Githany left, Bane realized that she had tricked him and she had used a lesser poison to cover a far more powerful toxin on her lips&mdash;[[Synox/Legends|synox]]. Though he attempted to strengthen himself by drinking in the suffering of those who died on a battlefield on Ambria, the dark side was too faint on the planet. Falling into unconsciousness, Bane collapsed. A small boy named [[Mikki]], along with his father and brothers, who were scavenging the battlefield, happened across Bane's lightsaber. Seeing his chance, Bane used the Force to control the lightsaber and kill the boys. In so doing, he absorbed the father's horror and suffering, using it to temporarily give him strength. Still feeding on the man's fear, Bane then killed him, ignoring his pleas for mercy.<ref name="pod" />

Strengthened by their pain, Bane was able to hold off the poison long enough to locate the healer [[Caleb]], who had come to the planet to help the victims of a recent battle. Upon finding the healer, Bane found that he refused to give the Sith Lord assistance. Infuriated, Bane considered forcing the man to help him, but found that his will was strong enough to resist the Sith Lord's mental prodding. However, Bane sensed the presence of another individual: [[Serra|Caleb's daughter]], and threatened to drop her into a boiling pot her unless the healer assisted him. Caleb relented and healed Bane, leaving him fully revitalized. Before departing for Ruusan, Bane considered killing Caleb, but decided against it, realizing that the man could be of use to him at a later date.<ref name="pod" />

===Ruusan and the destruction of the Sith===
{{Quote|The Brotherhood must be purged. The Sith must be destroyed and rebuilt.|Bane|<ref name="pod" />}}
Now healed, Bane headed for Ruusan, where he planned to initiate his plot to destroy Kaan's Brotherhood. During a tactical planning session among the Dark Lords, Bane revealed himself, much to the surprise of the Sith. Bane proceeded to mock Kaan and the other Sith, accusing them of acting like cowards and holding back from the true power of the dark side. He then offered an alternative method to defeat the Jedi: a Force Wave. Kaan agreed to Bane's plan, and at nightfall, Bane met the others atop a cliff overlooking the forest where the Jedi were hiding. Bane led the Sith in a ritual designed to concentrate the power of the dark side in one being&mdash;Bane&mdash;and unleash its power on the Jedi. With Bane as the conduit, the Sith Lords [[Sixth Battle of Ruusan|released]] a lightning storm upon the forest, causing an inferno. As the forest burned, the Jedi (barely able to flee when their commander sensed the danger) were forced to flee to the plains nearby to avoid destruction. However, before Bane could wipe out the Jedi, the ritual was cut short. Fearing the power that had been revealed to him, Kaan had ended the ceremony, using his connection to the other Dark Lords to pull them out as well, announcing that they would board their [[Speeder/Legends|speeders]] and defeat the Jedi using more conventional methods. Bane was furious and decided that by choosing personal extravagance instead of harmony with the dark, once and for all, the Brotherhood marked itself as unworthy and unable to truly serve the dark side. As Githany tried to justify Kaan's actions by claiming that this way was more fun, Bane realized that she was not fit to be his apprentice&mdash;she had been corrupted by Kaan.<ref name="pod" />

Kopecz was the last Sith to leave on his speeder, informing Bane that his loyalty to the dark side before the Brotherhood would not be accepted by the Sith Lords. Bane then traveled back to the Sith compound to continue his plan to destroy the Brotherhood. Arriving back in the deserted camp, Bane was confronted by Qordis, who offered his allegiance, claiming that he saw Bane's real purpose for coming to Ruusan. Bane was intrigued, until Qordis revealed that he could help Bane overthrow Kaan and seize control of the Brotherhood. The Dark Lord then informed the former Academy head that he was mistaken&mdash;he had come not to take control of the Brotherhood of Darkness, but to destroy it. He then attacked Qordis with the Force, wounding him. When Qordis begged Bane to let him die in lightsaber combat, claiming it was more honorable, Bane mocked him, and continued to [[Telekinesis/Legends#Choking powers|choke]] him until he died.<ref name="pod" />

After killing Qordis, Bane entered Kaan's tent, and contacted [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Adrianna Nyras]], who was in control of the [[Sith fleet (New Sith Wars)|Sith fleet]] stationed in orbit holding back the Jedi reinforcements. Bane ordered Admiral Nyras to engage the Jedi fleet, despite, indeed because of the fact that doing so would allow the Jedi reinforcements to reach the surface in [[Dropship/Legends|dropships]]. Nyras obeyed the Sith Lord's orders, and as the two fleets met, several smaller ships with Jedi onboard were able to reach the surface. The Jedi immediately came to the aid of Hoth, forcing the Sith to retreat from what had seemed like certain victory. When Kaan returned to the camp, Bane confronted him, admitting that he had ordered the Sith fleet to break their blockade. Bane suggested that a hopeless Kaan use the thought bomb to destroy the Army of Light while manipulating him to believe that he intended to take over the Brotherhood.<ref name="pod" />

Kaan then played his trump card, using a [[Mind trick/Legends|mind trick]] to convince Bane that the other Sith did not trust him, and that he was not fit to rule. Kaan planned to lead the Dark Lords to a cave, where they would lure the Jedi and then unleash the thought bomb to annihilate them and claim victory. He also ordered Bane to remain at camp; after the defeat of the Army of Light, Kaan planned to return and have the Sith Lords kill the powerful [[darksider]]. Unknown to Kaan, Bane was able to easily resist his mind tricks, and was merely feigning obedience. Bane fooled Kaan into believing he had been tricked, and also intentionally deceived Kaan into believing that he and the other Sith could survive the thought bomb. Kaan and the other members of his order made their way to a series of caves nearby, save for Kopecz and Githany who tried to escape, and planning to allow the Jedi to follow them. A number of Jedi followed the Sith, [[Seventh Battle of Ruusan|confronting]] them deep underground. However, the Jedi were unable to stop Kaan from detonating the thought bomb, which killed all the Force-sensitives in the cave. Several [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]] away, Bane sensed the bomb's detonation. The Brotherhood had been deceived by Bane into destruction. Unaware of Darth Bane's existence, the Jedi believed that all the Sith had died in the cave.<ref name="pod" />

[[File:Zannah_Before_Bane.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Bane encounters Zannah]]
However, though Bane had successfully executed his plan, he still needed an apprentice. Exploring the planet in the aftermath of the [[Ruusan campaign]], he encountered a young Force-sensitive girl named [[Darth Zannah/Legends|Zannah]]. Zannah had been taken to the planet by the Jedi several months earlier, but had been separated from them, and had spent all her time on Ruusan merely trying to survive. She had befriended a [[Bouncer]] named [[Laa (Bouncer)|Laa]], who helped protect her. However, two Jedi had mistakenly killed her friend, causing her to lash out in anger and kill them. Upon finding her, Bane sensed her Force potential, as well as the anger inside her. In addition, Zannah did not back down from Bane, and proclaimed herself to be a killer. Impressed,<ref name="pod" /> Bane informed the girl that she would become his apprentice.<ref name="two" />

===Rebuilding the Sith===
{{Quote|There are no other Sith. There never will be, except for us. One Master and one apprentice; one to embody the power, the other to crave it.|Bane, to Zannah|<ref name="two" />}}
[[File:Gamer-3-bane.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Darth Bane in Freedon Nadd's tomb on the moon Dxun.]]
Before departing Ruusan, the Dark Lord took his apprentice to the Sith camp, where a group of [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]] were looting the site. The mercenaries had fought for the Sith, only to abandon the cause after Kaan led his troops into the cave. Disgusted with those who were loyal only to money, Bane attacked the mercenaries, quickly killing four of them. Though the other two fled, Bane dismissed chasing them down because he saw no need in it; the two were soldiers for hire and thus would be believed by no one. Furthermore, Bane believed that the use of rumors of the Sith's continued existence could prove useful by confusing the Jedi Order and spreading fear and chaos.<ref name="two" />

In hopes of finding useful artifacts, Bane and Zannah searched the camp, finding a manuscript about the ancient Dark Lord [[Freedon Nadd]] that had belonged to Qordis. Qordis had added in notes of his own, indicating that Nadd was [[Tomb of Freedon Nadd#Dxun tomb|buried]] on the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Dxun/Legends|Dxun]]. Also in the document were sequences of numbers; Bane realized that these were account numbers where Qordis had kept his wealth, of which he had a great deal. With the manuscript in his possession, Bane left the camp, taking Zannah with him to the site of the thought bomb's detonation. He also began explaining to her some of the tenets of his new Rule of Two, such as the [[Code of the Sith/Legends|Sith Code]]. In the cave, the two encountered Zannah's cousin, [[Darovit]]. The two embraced, only for Zannah to quickly pull away upon remembering that she was now a Sith. When she explained this to her cousin, he challenged Bane to fight, despite the fact that he was a mere boy and no match for the Dark Lord. However, before Bane could kill him, Zannah used the dark side to cause his hand to explode. Though Bane recognized that his apprentice had only attacked the boy to save him from Bane by rendering him cast down, he saw no harm in letting him go, and was aware that Zannah was only a neophyte in the ways of the dark side and that her early application of Sith ideals to get what she wanted needed to be rewarded and cultivated. Bane decided to travel to Dxun in hopes of discovering even greater power. He instructed Zannah to meet him on the neighboring planet [[Onderon/Legends|Onderon]] in two weeks time, and then departed, leaving his apprentice on Ruusan to find her own way, in the process and prove herself.<ref name="two" />

After leaving Ruusan, Bane headed for Dxun in the ''Valcyn''. However, while in transit, the ghostly spirit of Qordis, a hallucination resulting from the Thought Bomb damaging Bane's brain, appeared and chided him for abandoning the Brotherhood. Bane insisted that he was only furthering the Sith cause, but he was enraged by Qordis's claims. After spending several days stuck in the starfighter's cockpit listening to Qordis curse him, Bane finally released his anger when the ''Valcyn'' entered Dxun's [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]]. Unleashing a blast of dark side energy, he caused Qordis's spirit to vanish, but also damaged the ship, forcing him to make a crash-landing.<ref name="two" />

Bane, however, managed to survive the crash even though his ship was destroyed upon impacting the moon. Though Qordis continued to mock him, insisting that he would die on Dxun, Bane ignored his pleas, and marched onwards to where he sensed Nadd's tomb to be. Though he was attacked by a predator on the way, the Sith Lord managed to defeat it and continue on to his goal. Bane was guided by the spirit of Kaan, also a hallucination who, unlike Qordis, did not make any attempts to attack him. He was able to make it to the tomb and immediately began searching it. There, Bane located Nadd's holocron. However, as Bane moved to claim it, he was attacked by a number of [[Beetle/Legends|beetle]]-like creatures in the chamber where the holocron was. Bane was unable to keep them away, and two of them attached to his skin (square in the chest and the back of his left shoulder). As they could not be removed, this caused the Sith Lord to be in a perpetual state of pain from the creatures gnawing on his skin, only enhanced as they began to slowly multiply and spread across his body.<ref name="two" />

As he began to study Nadd's holocron, Bane discovered that the creatures were parasites called [[orbalisk]]s that could not be removed. Though they caused the Dark Lord to be in constant pain, their shells were impenetrable; even lightsabers could not crack them. The orbalisks covering nearly all of Bane's body formed an impervious suit of [[Armor/Legends|armor]]. Furthermore, they gave Bane tremendous healing abilities, and pumped chemicals into his [[Blood/Legends|bloodstream]], enhancing his connection to the Force while increasing his rage, thus boosting his power in battle. Because they increased his capabilities while causing him to suffer unending pain, Bane viewed the creatures as both a gift and a curse. After spending days studying from the holocron, Bane exited the tomb and used the power the orbalisks gave him to attack the hallucinations, making them disappear. He then headed to Onderon. Taming a flying [[drexl]] using the powers of the dark side, he mounted it and rode towards the edge of the atmosphere where Dxun came close to Onderon's atmosphere. Once on Onderon he found Zannah being threatened by a group of [[Beast Riders]]. Onboard the drexl, Bane attacked the Riders, slaughtering them and their mounts. Now that his apprentice had proven herself, Bane planned to begin training Zannah.<ref name="two" />

===Zannah's apprenticeship===
{{Quote|Information is a commodity. It can be traded, sold, and purchased. And in the end, credits are only as useful as the secrets they can buy.|Bane|<ref name="two" />}}
[[File:DarthBane-NEGTC.png|thumb|left|200px|Darth Bane wearing his orbalisk armor]]
Bane and Zannah acquired a new vessel from a Neimoidian [[Merchant/Legends|merchant]] and left Onderon, establishing a camp on Ambria, where they spent the next ten years. Thanks to the credits they had obtained from Qordis's account, the two built up a vast intelligence network, learning secrets that they hoped would one day allow them to destroy the Jedi and gain [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] control. The Sith Lord used the false name [[Lord Eddels]], a hold over from Qordis's fake name when setting up the bank accounts. Bane taught Zannah in the ways of the dark side as well as the philosophy of the Rule of Two. Future Sith Lords were to be taught the virtues of patience, cunning, and secrecy, and each was to take on the title of Darth,<ref name="two" /> a tradition that dated back to the time of the [[Jedi Civil War]] nearly three millennia earlier.<ref name="pod" /> Around this time, Sith [[Prisoner/Legends|prisoners]] in custody on [[Akrit'tar/Legends|Akrit'tar]] revealed to the Jedi that they believed Bane to be the fabled [[Sith'ari/Legends|Sith'ari]], although the Jedi incorrectly believed that Bane had been killed during the Ruusan campaign. The [[Jedi archivist/Legends|Jedi archivist]] [[Restelly Quist/Legends|Restelly Quist]] wrote about Bane in the Jedi training manual [[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force|''The Jedi Path'']], stating that he was a champion of the Sith who, like the rest of the Brotherhood, had failed.<ref name="TJP">[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force (real-life book)|''The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force'']]</ref> Along with studying the dark side, Zannah was tasked with occasionally stirring up rebel groups on different worlds over the years, in order to distract the Republic. He was careful to always instruct his apprentice to cause these groups to be defeated, as while he wanted the Republic distracted and weakened, he did not want one of these separatist groups gaining enough power to overthrow the Republic itself.<ref name="two" />

In [[990 BBY]],<ref name="Serenno date">The events of ''[[Darth Bane: Rule of Two]]'' that feature the [[kidnap attempt on Serenno]] take place ten [[Standard year/Legends|years]] after the [[Seventh Battle of Ruusan]], which ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates to [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]].</ref> Zannah undertook a mission to [[Serenno/Legends|Serenno]], where she manipulated the [[Anti-Republic Liberation Front]] and their plans to [[Kidnap attempt on Serenno|kidnap]] former [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Tarsus Valorum/Legends|Tarsus Valorum]], leading to them failing in their mission. She returned from Serenno with a Force-sensitive nobleman named [[Hetton]], and his eight [[Sith assassin/Legends|Umbaran Shadow Assassins]]. The assassins [[Duel on Ambria (990 BBY)|attacked]] the Dark Lord, although Bane was able to defeat them and kill Hetton. He then attacked his apprentice in a mindless rage, nearly killing her. Zannah saved herself only by revealing that it had been a trick to kill Hetton and gain information he possessed&mdash;the location of the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]] planet [[Tython/Legends|Tython]], home to an ancient fortress of the Dark Lord [[Belia Darzu]]. Hetton claimed there was information there on how to create holocrons, something Bane was very interested in, as he had tried and failed several times, including two initial attempts after learning the meaning of the [[Rituals of Invocation|ritual glyphs]] on [[Sith holocron/Legends|Sith holocrons]], and a final failure while Zannah was on Serenno.<ref name="two" />

Bane [[Mission to Tython|traveled]] to Tython, sending his apprentice in disguise to the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] in the meantime. Bane had begun to wonder if the orbalisks could be holding him back, and he wanted her to research possible ways of removing them. On Tython, Bane located Darzu's fortress, and although he had to battle an army of Darzu's [[technobeast]]s, he was able to claim the holocron. From it he learned the secret to creating a successful holocron of his own. However, shortly after this triumph, Zannah landed on Tython along with her cousin Darovit. Darovit had revealed the Sith's existence to the Jedi, and had been taken to the Jedi Temple to speak with the [[Jedi Council/Legends|council]]. In the archives he had encountered Zannah, whom he recognized as his childhood friend despite her disguise. The two had fled after Darovit revealed to her that he had informed the Jedi of their existence.<ref name="two" />

===Battle on Tython===
{{Quote|Inside the fortress. The Jedi have found us.|Bane|<ref name="two" />}}
[[File:Duel_on_Tython.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The Duel on Tython]]
After informing her master that the Jedi had followed her, Zannah and Bane prepared for [[Duel on Tython|battle]] in Darzu's ancient fortress. Though they were outnumbered, the Sith were able to gain the upper hand, thanks to the ferocity of Bane's fighting style and the advantages accorded him by his orbalisk armor. Zannah was able to kill [[Raskta Lsu]] and [[Sarro Xaj]], while Bane killed [[Valenthyne Farfalla]] and fatally wounded [[Worror Dowmat]]. However, as he moved in to kill the last Jedi, [[Johun Othone]], with Force lightning, Worror created a [[Protection bubble]] to deflect Bane's Force lightning back on him, frying the Sith Lord and killing the orbalisks. In response, the parasites released a deadly poison that threatened to kill Bane. Zannah quickly ended Othone, and took Bane to her [[Loranda (starship)|ship]]. Recalling what Bane had once told her, she decided to take him to Caleb on Ambria, bringing Darovit with her.<ref name="two" />

However, the healer refused to cooperate, and as his daughter now lived on another world, Zannah had no leverage over him. Prodded by Darovit, who insisted that she was a good person, not a Sith, and by Caleb, who promised to heal Bane if she gave up herself and her master to the Jedi, Zannah agreed to surrender, and sent a message to the Jedi Temple, informing the Jedi that the Sith Lord who had killed a number of Jedi on Tython was on Ambria, helpless. Caleb then began to heal Bane. When Bane awoke days later he was free of the orbalisks and cured of their poison. Zannah told him what she had done, and he expressed his disappointment before asking her to kill him, sparing him the life of a prisoner of the Jedi. However, Zannah had had another plan in mind all along. She killed Caleb, and then used her [[Sith sorcery/Legends|power]] to [[Summon fear|drive Darovit mad]].<ref name="two" />

[[Ambria strike team|The Jedi]] soon came ready to arrest the Sith, but Zannah had [[Spell of concealment|hidden]] herself and her master under the hut. All they found was Darovit, who, in his madness, [[Confrontation on Ambria|attacked]] the Jedi. They killed him easily, believing he was the Sith. At long last, the Jedi thought they had finally eliminated the Sith. When Bane awoke, he grabbed his student by her neck in a fury, thinking he was captured by the Jedi, but Zannah told him of what had happened, and he admitted that he had underestimated her, and was proud of her. One day, he told her, she would have the power to overthrow him and take an apprentice of her own.<ref name="two" />

===New worries===
{{Quote|Show me the ritual of essence transfer.|Bane, to Andeddu's holocron|<ref name="doe" />}}
By [[980 BBY]], Bane and Zannah had relocated to [[Ciutric IV]], where they owned a large [[Darth Bane's mansion|mansion]]. The two possessed immense wealth, which they used to continue to build up their network of [[Spy/Legends|spies]] and plan for the time when the Sith could destroy the Jedi. Bane had also created a [[Darth Bane's holocron|holocron]] which held all of his knowledge, and, posing as a simple collector, the Dark Lord had acquired a great number of Sith artifacts. However, Bane was worried about his apprentice. Because she showed no desire to claim the mantle of Dark Lord of the Sith, he had begun to believe that she was weak, and planned to wait for him to age before she challenged him, rather than seizing power from the Dark Lord when he was strong, as the Rule of Two demanded. By postponing the inevitable duel between master and apprentice, Zannah, Bane believed, was destroying the purpose of the Rule of Two&mdash;to keep the Sith strong. Further worrying him was the fact that he was aging rapidly due to his use of the dark side, and his injuries on Tython a decade ago. As such, Bane had begun to develop contingency plans, based on something he had stumbled upon in a book&mdash;according to record, an ancient Sith Lord named [[Darth Andeddu]] had lived for centuries, thanks to his use of the dark side of the Force. Though there was very little information available, Bane was determined to learn Andeddu's secret and save the Sith.<ref name="doe" />

[[File:ZannahRuleOfTwo.jpg|thumb|left|225px|Darth Bane with his apprentice, Darth Zannah]]
One afternoon, Bane&mdash;under the guise of a wealthy merchant named "Sepp Omek"&mdash;arranged a meeting with [[Argel Tenn]], an authority on Sith artifacts, at a local cantina. The Sith Lord despised the man, who believed himself to be an expert on the Sith, when Bane was confident that Tenn knew nothing of the true power of the dark side. Nonetheless, Tenn was useful, and so the Sith Lord had utilized his assistance multiple times in the past to acquire Sith relics. Bane had asked Tenn to find information on Darth Andeddu, and after a great deal of searching, Tenn had located an ancient manuscript on Andeddu, which he sold to the Dark Lord.<ref name="doe" />

The text revealed that there was a [[Andeddu's Keep|fortress]] dedicated to Andeddu on the Deep Core world of [[Prakith/Legends|Prakith]]. Bane decided to [[Mission to Doan|send]] Zannah to the planet [[Doan]]&mdash;where a Jedi had been murdered three days ago&mdash;to determine who had been able to kill the Jedi, while he planned to surreptitiously travel to Prakith, and learn the secret to immortality. After Zannah departed, Bane boarded his starship, the [[Triumph (Theta-class T-1 vessel)|''Triumph'']], and [[Mission to Prakith (Darth Bane)|headed]] to Prakith, where he located Andeddu's fortress. Upon entering, he was attacked by members of the [[Sith cult/Legends|cult]] [[Malevolence (cult)|Malevolence]], dedicated to the long-dead Andeddu. Bane was able easily slay the assailants, and recover [[Holocron of Heresies|Andeddu's holocron]]. On the return trip, Bane accessed the holocron, but found that the [[Gatekeeper/Legends|gatekeeper]] was unwilling to teach him how to live on after death. Angered, he forced it to tell him&mdash;by plunging his consciousness into the holocron, he was able to literally take the knowledge from the device, thus learning the art of [[essence transfer]]. Using the dark side, he could transfer his spirit into another's body. Though this ritual was extremely dangerous, Bane was convinced that his will was strong enough to overpower his target.<ref name="doe" />

===Ambush===
{{Quote|I want him to see what it's like to be helpless and afraid. I want him to know what it's like to be a victim. I want him to understand that what he did to my father&mdash;to me&mdash;was wrong!|Serra|<ref name="doe" />}}
When Bane returned to Ciutric IV, he found that Zannah was not back. Upon entering his mansion, he was [[Skirmish in Darth Bane's mansion|attacked]] by a Force-sensitive [[Darth Cognus|Iktotchi]] and a group of soldiers. Bane fought back, and was able to kill several of the assailants. However, the [[Iktotchi/Legends|Iktotchi]] was able to stab him with a blade coated in [[senflax]], a powerful neurotoxin designed to knock out even the strongest of opponents. The toxin caused him to faint, enabling the Iktotchi and the soldiers to take him prisoner. Bane was taken to Doan, where their benefactor, [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] Serra, resided. Serra was the daughter of the healer Caleb, and upon learning of her father's death at the hands of a Sith Lord, sought to punish the guilty party. Deep in the [[Stone Prison]], Serra began to torture Bane by administering various poisons. However, much to her shock, Bane insisted he had not killed Caleb. Nonetheless, Serra reiterated that it was still his fault, and continued torturing him, expecting the Dark Lord to beg for mercy and forgiveness. However, Bane was not overcome from the pain&mdash;far from it. Instead, he explained that Caleb had died because he was weak, and that Bane himself had been captured because he was not strong enough. Feeding on his own pain and Serra's anger, Bane mocked the Princess, and proclaimed that he would escape. Furious, Serra injected him with senflax, knocking him out, before leaving the prison.<ref name="doe" />

[[File:DarthBane-DoE.png|thumb|right|180px|Darth Bane]]
Unknown to Serra, her [[Bodyguard/Legends|bodyguard]], [[Lucia (soldier)|Lucia]], had served with Dessel in the New Sith Wars, and was stunned at the anger and cruelty her mistress was showing. Lucia made the decision to free Bane, believing she still owed him her life for his heroics during the war. She injected him with a chemical that would cancel out the effects of the senflax and allow Bane to break free. When Bane awoke, he found that his strength had returned, and he was able to escape from his cell, leaving several guards dead in the process. As Bane headed upwards, he sensed Zannah's presence. The Sith apprentice had managed to track him to Doan, and had come prepared to kill him and take the title of Dark Lord. She had learned of his interest in Andeddu, and believed that he intended to use the dark side to prevent himself from ever dying, and rule over the Sith for eternity&mdash;exactly the opposite, she believed, of what the Rule of Two was created for.<ref name="doe" />

As Bane headed for a hangar, he encountered Lucia. She quickly explained who she was, and begged him to let Serra live. Hesitating for a moment, Bane then exclaimed that the soldier she had known was no more, and prepared to execute Lucia. Before he could unleash the dark side on her, Zannah arrived, and killed Lucia with a mighty Force push. She proclaimed that Bane was weak, and unwilling to let his knowledge pass on to her. Bane countered that his apprentice was not ready, and was unworthy of the mantle of Dark Lord of the Sith. Bane tried to conjure an illusion of himself being armed, but he was no talent as an illusionist. Realizing that Bane's lightsaber had been taken from him, Zannah then [[Duel on Doan|attacked]]. Bane was able to goad her into fighting like a brute and so hold her off with the Force, though he was aware that he could not defeat Zannah without a lightsaber, and was merely delaying the end. Suddenly, alarm bells rang out&mdash;Serra had activated the prison's self-destruct sequence. As the prison began to collapse, Bane used Force lightning against a bomb to bring the ceiling down. Though Zannah was able to avoid being crushed, a wall of rock now stood between the two. Zannah fled to her ship, while Bane ran toward the main hangar, where he found the Iktotchi. As he prepared to attack her, she bowed to him, holding out his lightsaber.<ref name="doe" />

The woman then explained that she sensed his power, and wanted to become his apprentice to find a purpose in life. Realizing her strength in the Force, and her determination to become a Sith, he accepted. The two boarded her [[Stalker (shuttle)|starship]] and left as the prison collapsed around them. The Iktotchi then explained that she was an assassin who had been able to track Bane to Ciutric IV thanks to visions she received through the Force. Guided by another vision of hers, the two headed to Ambria. There, Bane found Serra, who had been able to escape the destruction of the prison and had fled to her homeworld. Having abandoned her desire for revenge, she tried in vain to convince Bane and the Iktotchi to turn away from the dark side, only for the Iktotchi to kill her. Bane prepared to begin training his new apprentice, now known as Darth Cognus. However, one loose end remained: Zannah. The Dark Lord sent a communication to [[Victory (Theta-class T-1 vessel)|Zannah's shuttle]], instructing her to come to Ambria. She complied, and soon arrived for their [[Duel on Ambria (980 BBY)|final confrontation]].<ref name="doe" />

===Duel to the death===
{{Quote|I have surpassed you, Bane. Now I am the Master."''<br />''"Then prove it.|Zannah and Bane|<ref name="doe" />}}
[[File:2nd_Battle_of_Ambria.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Zannah and Bane duel on Ambria.]]
After Zannah landed on Ambria and disembarked from her shuttle, Bane walked towards her to meet her.  Cognus watched the two Sith Lords prepare for combat, as she understood that she was not to interfere in the battle. After Bane told Zannah that Cognus had joined the dark side, Cognus told Zannah that if Zannah defeated Bane, she would swear her loyalty to Zannah as her apprentice. The two Sith Lords then drew their lightsabers and engaged in combat.<ref name="doe" /> 

Knowing that the loser would die, both fought furiously, with Bane slowly pushing Zannah back. Zannah then unleashed her Sith sorcery, only to have Bane successfully repel her attack on his mind. The dueling Sith clashed blades and fought while Force-empowering themselves. Bane gained the upper hand, forcing Zannah, wounded, to back off via flamboyant Force use on her part. As Bane charged forward, ready to take her life, Zannah played her trump card, creating deadly [[dark side tendrils]] by the dark power of the planet's caged darkness. One of these tendrils brushed against Bane, causing him to feel pain unlike anything he had ever known. Managing to stay conscious, he was able to attack Zannah and swiftly disarm her. As the Dark Lord prepared to kill his apprentice, a tendril lunged up, grabbing his arm and vaporizing it. The tendrils were impervious to Bane's violet lightning bolts. With no other option and in his last act, Bane released his essence, determined now to destroy Zannah's consciousness and take control of her body. The power of the ritual of essence transfer destroyed Bane's body and turned it into ash.<ref name="doe" />

The two Sith Lords battled within Zannah's mind, fighting for possession of her body. Their wills battled where once blade and keen impulses had, each trying to push the other out and into the great [[Chaos/Legends|void]] from which there was no return. Bane's essence occupied Zannah's body, rooting in, and he could see from Zannah's eyes, and hear with her ears. After a struggle of wills, it was over -- Zannah had triumphed, and Bane was dead. However, a small portion of her master's essence remained in Zannah, just enough to make her hand quake like his did.<ref name="doe" /><ref name="dkw">{{WebCite|url=http://www.drewkarpyshyn.com/spoiler.htm|text=Dynasty of Evil Spoiler Alert!|work=[[Drew Karpyshyn]]'s [http://www.drewkarpyshyn.com official website]|archivedate=20200729020745}}</ref>

===Legacy===
{{Quote|Power is its ''own'' purpose. To ''share'' it is to ''dilute'' it. You delude yourself, pretender—your order will yet turn on itself and you.|Bane's holocron addresses Darth Krayt|<ref name="broken 4">[[Legacy (2006) 5|''Legacy'' (2006) 5]]</ref>}}
Following Bane's death, Zannah took Cognus as her apprentice, continuing the Rule of Two.<ref name="doe" /> Nearly a thousand years later, in [[181 BBY/Legends|181 BBY]], the [[Dark Jedi/Legends|fallen]] [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Kibh Jeen]] revealed to the Jedi with his dying words the survival of the Sith and the Rule of Two.<ref name="Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref> However, believing Bane's plan had been destroyed along with his death,<ref name="Encyclopedia">{{SWE|characters|darth-bane|Darth Bane}}</ref> the Jedi considered this nothing more than gibberish<ref name="pena">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/insideronline/88/indexp2.html|text=''Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties''|int=Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties}}</ref> and presumed the Sith to have been wiped out.<ref name="Encyclopedia" />

[[File:Darth_Bane_TCW.png|thumb|right|250px|Darth Bane's specter on Korriban]]
In [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], the Jedi learned that the Sith were not extinct<ref name="tpm">{{Film|I}}</ref> and were later the cause behind the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]<ref name="aotc">{{Film|II}}</ref> in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]]. Sometime during [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]], [[Dooku/Legends|Darth Tyranus]] shared ''The Rule of Two'' with [[Quinlan Vos/Legends|Quinlan Vos]] in an ill-conceived effort to further corrupt the Jedi.<ref name="BoS">''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]''</ref> The [[Lightsaber crystal/Legends|lightsaber crystal]] [[Bane's Heart (crystal)|Bane's Heart]], which had been created by Bane and given to Zannah, fell into the possession of the [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg]] warrior [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]] almost a millennium after the Dark Lord's death.<ref name="cswe">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref>

In the year [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]],<ref>{{TCWdates|613}}</ref> the [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] of the Jedi Order [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] traveled to Korriban on a journey to learn the gift of [[Force ghost/Legends|manifesting]] life after death. When he entered one of the temples located in the Valley of the Dark Lords, Yoda discovered a [[Tomb of Darth Bane/Legends|tomb]] that had been built for Bane. A giant, smoldering specter of Bane then emerged from a sarcophagus and tried to tempt the Jedi Master into becoming his apprentice. However, Yoda declared the specter of Bane to be nothing but an illusion with nothing to offer him, and the fiery ghost disappeared.<ref name="Sacrifice">{{TCW|Sacrifice (episode)}}</ref>

In [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]],<ref name="SWGA">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]''</ref> Bane's dream was realized, and his Rule of Two validated, when the Sith under [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] and [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] finally achieved [[Galactic Empire/Legends|control]] over the galaxy and nearly [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|wiped out]] the Jedi Order.<ref name="rots">{{Film|III}}</ref> Darth Bane was the legendary Sith'ari, an individual who had been prophesied to restore the Sith to glory. Because of the Sith Order Bane had forged a millennium earlier, the prophecy ultimately came true.<ref name="cswe" /> In [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]],<ref name="0BBYDate">The events of "[[Resurrection (comic story)|Resurrection]]," during which the [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtrooper]] [[Captain/Legends|captain]] [[Death/Legends|dies]] on [[Kalakar Six]], take place before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], which ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates to [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], and after the theft of the [[Death Star plans/Legends|Death Star plans]] by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]], which took place during the [[Battle of Toprawa]] per ''[[Jedi Dawn]]''. Since the novel [[Death Star (novel)|''Death Star'']] establishes that the latter battle took place following the [[attack on the first Death Star]], which ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' in turn dates to 0 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|BBY]], the Battle of Toprawa must have also occured in 0 BBY, meaning the events of "Resurrection" are set in that [[Standard year/Legends|year]], as well.</ref> a faction known as the [[Prophets of the Dark Side]] revealed themselves to Vader and [[Duel on Kalakar Six|unleashed]] a resurrected [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]], who believed that Vader was not of "the blood of Bane" and sought to retake his place at Sidious's side. However, Vader managed to overcome his predecessor, affirming his station among the Sith.<ref name="Resurrection">{{Tales|9|Resurrection (comic story)}}</ref>

In [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]],<ref name="SWGA" /> however, the Sith's victory was undone when Darth Vader, who redeemed himself back into the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] Anakin Skywalker, killed Sidious during the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]] to save his son [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] before expiring from his injuries, bringing Bane's established Sith lineage to an end.<ref name="rotj">{{Film|VI}}</ref> Like Bane,<ref name="doe" /> Sidious was able to learn the power of essence transfer and used it to survive his first death to then transfer his spirit into fresh [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] bodies he could use to rule a [[Dark Empire|new empire]] to fight against the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]].<ref name="de">[[Dark Empire 2|''Dark Empire'' 2]]</ref> However, Sidious was finally killed by Skywalker and his friends and his spirit was caught within the dying Jedi Knight [[Empatojayos Brand]] and then as Brand perished, cast to Chaos so he would never return ever again, which meant the definitive ending of Bane's Order of the Sith Lords.<ref name="e'se">[[Empire's End 2|''Empire's End'' 2]]</ref>

Bane's holocron eventually fell into the hands of [[Darth Krayt]]. In [[137 ABY]], it was accessed, along with those of [[Darth Nihilus]] and Darth Andeddu, on Korriban by Krayt. The new Dark Lord wished to learn from Bane's experience with the parasitic orbalisks, and how he could survive his own infection by [[Yuuzhan Vong]] organisms. Bane however chastised Krayt for not following the Rule of Two and considered the One Sith as heretics, telling Krayt his new [[Rule of One]] would be the very undoing of the ways of the Sith itself.<ref name="broken 4" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Equality is a lie&hellip; A myth to appease the masses. Simply look around and you will see the lie for what it is! There are those with power, those with the strength and will to lead. And there are those meant to follow&mdash;those incapable of anything but servitude and a meager, worthless existence.<br />''"''Equality is a perversion of the natural order!&hellip; It binds the strong to the weak. They become anchors that drag the exceptional down to mediocrity. Individuals destined and deserving of greatness have it denied them. They suffer for the sake of keeping them even with their inferiors.<br />''"''Equality is a chain, like obedience. Like fear or uncertainty or self doubt.|Bane|<ref name="two" />}}
[[File:DarthBane-frontal.jpg|thumb|left|220px|Darth Bane, the Sith'ari and the founder of the Rule of Two]]
Bane was extremely dedicated to the Sith cause, and was determined to bring about the end of the Jedi, though he knew he might not live to see it.<ref name="two" /> He was a firm believer in the rule of the strong, viewing the weak as chains holding back the strong. According to the natural order of things, Bane believed, the weak should serve the strong, rather than being treated as equals. Whereas the Jedi and the Republic believed that it was the duty of the strong to help the weak, Bane believed that the strong were intended to rule the weak masses. Equality, Bane believed, was a lie perpetuated by the Jedi. One of the reasons he hated the Brotherhood was that it supported equality amongst the Sith.<ref name="pod" /> Bane's Rule of Two was designed with the intention of strengthening the Sith Order over time, with each apprentice challenging their master for the title of Dark Lord. If the apprentice failed, the master would ideally find another apprentice. In this way, each successive Dark Lord would be stronger than their predecessor. Darth Bane imparted his beliefs, particularly his theory of rule of the strong, to Zannah. After he dueled Hetton and received no assistance from his apprentice, Bane confronted her, asking why she had not helped him. She replied that she knew that Bane would be able to kill the man and his assassins, and if he was unable to do so, then he was weak and unworthy of his title of Dark Lord. Bane was pleased with this explanation, stating that she was correct&mdash;only the strongest could survive.<ref name="two" />

Another problem Bane saw in the structure of the Brotherhood was its inclusion of numerous Sith. He was convinced that the Sith's greatest strength&mdash;their ambition&mdash; was also their greatest weakness, and would be checked by the Rule of Two. With a multitude of Sith, he felt that it was practically inevitable that they would constantly be fighting amongst themselves, leaving them unable to focus on their true foe, the Jedi. Additionally, he believed that the power of the dark side was finite, and that the existence of many Sith spread the power of the dark side thin. By creating a system that allowed for the existence of only two Sith Lords at any one time, Bane believed that he could keep the Sith strong and safe from the Jedi.<ref name="pod" /> Many centuries after his death, his holocron's gatekeeper mocked Darth Krayt for abandoning the Rule of Two for his Rule of One, telling the "pretender" that his Order would destroy itself as so many similarly structured Sith Orders had.<ref name="broken 4" />

Bane's philosophy caused him to view Skere Kaan and the other Sith of his time as fools, and he believed that as long as the Brotherhood of Darkness existed, the Sith would be unable to triumph over the Jedi. He even went so far as to label the leader of the Brotherhood, Kaan, a coward unworthy of the title Dark Lord of the Sith. He eventually defied Kaan by refusing the order to report to Ruusan, instead stealing Qordis's starship and heading to Lehon, where he hoped to learn from Darth Revan, who he considered to be a true master of the dark side. To symbolize that his new Sith Order was different from the Brotherhood, Bane revived the title of Darth, which Kaan had discouraged by claiming that it was antiquated and encouraged unnecessary competition among the Sith.<ref name="pod" /> In a similar vein, Bane thought poorly of Sith amulets, viewing them as little more than magic toys to be kept away from others when compared to his powers as a great master of the Sith ways.<ref name="doe" />

Later in his life, the Dark Lord sought the secrets to achieving immortality. He did this not because he feared death, but simply because he believed that Zannah was too weak to claim his title. Bane suspected that his apprentice was waiting until he was old and weak to challenge him, at which point she could easily defeat him. However, were she to do this, she would not prove her superiority, as was necessitated by the Rule of Two. To ensure the Sith's survival, Bane undertook his search for the fabled Darth Andeddu. Ultimately, Zannah proved herself a worthy successor when she killed Bane.<ref name="doe" />

[[File:DarthBaneEGTF.jpg|thumb|right|220px|Bane's cunning and vision made him a transformative figure in Sith history.]]
Bane learned hatred and anger at an early age, as he grew up with a father who hated him. Bane, in turn, despised Hurst, who frequently insulted and beat him. After Bane challenged him, only to have Hurst nearly kill him in response, an irate Bane later killed his father through unconscious use of the Force. He took to the dark side with ease, at first, although the Human lost his faith after realizing that he was responsible for his father's death and wondering about the killing of Fohargh. Afraid of the dark side, he pulled away, only to regain his confidence with the assistance of the ancient Sith in the form of texts. From there, Bane grew strong, quickly surpassing even Lord Kaan.<ref name="pod" /> With the dark side as his ally, he founded a new Sith Order, one based on secrecy and rule of the strong.<ref name="two" /> Bane possessed an extremely strong will. On multiple occasions when severely wounded, he refused to surrender, using the power of the dark side to fuel himself and keep fighting.

Bane bore a vitriolic hatred for beings like Argel Tenn, who considered themselves masters of the dark side but in fact were unable to use the Force. The Dark Lord desired to reveal his true identity and power to Tenn, whom he felt knew nothing of the dark side's true power, but knew that to do so would be foolish. He viewed being kidnapped by Serra's people as a mark of weakness and he stopped for a moment when breaking out when Lucia called him by his original name and he did not understand her intent. By that time, his memories of his time as a military man were dim and he never thought of how he would react to meeting a fellow Gloom Walker.<ref name="doe" /> A practical man, Bane found no value in wealth or other material possessions beyond their use to the Sith cause of getting more power, believing that the worth of an object was directly correlated to its usefulness. He even believed that Sith like Qordis were foolish to care so much for such things. Upon his acquisition of Qordis's vast wealth, he used it only to further the Sith cause.<ref name="two" /> He also did not believe in the concept of honorable death, viewing honor as a fool's prize. Though he was absolutely ruthless and never hesitated to kill when he believed it necessary, Bane was very disdainful of those who killed without purpose, viewing those who enjoyed killing as barbarous, perverse fools. In accordance with this philosophy, Bane allowed Caleb to live after their initial meeting in 1000 BBY<ref name="pod" />&mdash;in fact, Caleb would heal him from near-death years later. Still, Bane was willing to kill without a second thought, and did so on many occasions.<ref name="two" />

Despite his bond with the dark side of the Force, Bane did have feelings for Githany when the two were pupils on Korriban. She returned these feelings, and Bane sought to make her his apprentice after becoming convinced that the Brotherhood was irrevocably flawed. However, when she proved herself to be unworthy in his eyes by proclaiming Kaan's virtues, he abandoned these thoughts, and left her to perish with the rest of the Brotherhood. Nonetheless, Bane found himself pleased to see her when they met on Ambria a short time later, with her as Kaan's emissary; even as when she proved unable to see his ideals, he left her to be slain by the disaster that would claim the Brotherhood.<ref name="pod" />

==Powers and abilities==
===Lightsaber combat===
{{Quote|In the end I think you'll find this lightsaber will suit your personal style quite well.|Kas'im, upon handing Na'daz's old lightsaber to Bane|<ref name="pod" />}}
[[File:DarthBaneLightsaber-CSWE.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Darth Bane's lightsaber.]]
Darth Bane was trained in lightsaber combat by the Blademaster Kas'im. He became a deadly lightsaber duelist, and wielded a red-bladed, curved-hilt [[Darth Bane's lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] presented by the Twi'lek Dark Lord in recognition of his skill. Bane developed a slightly altered style with his unique weapon, the subtleties of which were recognized by only the most experienced weapon handlers. The leader of the Brotherhood of Darkness, Kaan, considered Bane to be the greater swordsman.<ref name="pod" />

As Dessel, Bane was able to win a fight with another miner by biting off his thumb (the other man was later set to be healed), and when attacked by three solders he was able to win a fistfight in the dark--killing one after stealing his dagger--by his brawn and flashes of the Force. As a soldier he also knocked out his CO with a single punch.<ref name="pod" />

Once he became a Sith student, he was selected to learn Form V combat. As a student, he won the majority of the challenges he took part it. By blade and Force he slew another student but lost to Sirak when he did not use the Force to fight better. He only lived after being beaten into the dirt after getting intense medical care. Still, Ka’seem in secret taught him to develop his saber skills once he started to use the Force again and he felt that he could fight for hours. Bane then defeated Sirak in a rainy duel when he had returned to the dark side and using it to probe his style and suddenly rush him with Force-augmented movement, destroying the other's sword and breaking his bones. When he was going through tombs of Moraband, he killed eight of twelve Tuk'ata who set upon him. He caught Force lightning from Sirak, then used his saber to defeat and behead his rival, while Githany slew the other two assassins.<ref name="pod" />

For all his skill and new power in the Force, he nearly died fighting Ka'seem. When they dueled on Lehon, Bane was able to hold off the other Sith and even begin to win with the Force's aid, only for the master of blades to reveal himself as a liar, a master of Jar'Kai and quite willing to tear Bane apart with his now twin blades. Darth Bane tactically used the layout of the Temple of the Ancients but had to flee. In the end, he only won because his enemy let himself be lured into a bad spot and Bane used a storm telekinesis and lightning that, though unable to break his mentor's Force wall, tore the walls down around him, crushing him. Then Bane collapsed after the effort of the battle.<ref name="pod" /> On Russan, he butchered a group of Sith thralls who he found with forms five and three, deflecting shots as needed. Duxon proved a nearly deadly test, when a massive cat-like creature attacked him and he only had the time to rally and hack it apart since the beast got confused by him. Soon after, he failed to knock aside all the orbalisks who set upon him when he raided Nadd's tomb, his saberwork and Force powers still letting a couple through, where they would latch and change his life.<ref name="two" />

After Bane acquired his lightsaber-impervious orbalisk armor, he soon adapted to the need to fight in the armor. While he often fought on foot, he could [[Mounted lightsaber combat|fight from atop an animal]], such as when on Onderon he deflected a volley of blaster bolts from himself and his thralled flying drexl. He favored a furious, all-offensive style of [[Form V/Legends|Djem So]], and capitalized on his tremendous physical strength to overwhelm opponents. When a group of Sith Shadow Assassins jumped him, he smote one in half, cleaved down two more, and chopped down another, despite being ambushed and zapped by their spears. Then he blocked a lightning bolt from and hacked the offending hand off the group's employer, Hetton and ran him through. Then he attacked his student, thinking she had betrayed him. He landed many hits with his limbs and disarmed her before she was able to reveal her true faithfulness. In his raid on Belia Darzu's fortress, he fought a horde of techno-virus tainted monsters and thralls to get at, at one point chopping the legs off a robotized rancor and brought it down. The man had to battle for more than an hour, before purging all the techobeasts, though he had to use most of his Force energy to keep himself from getting tired and even still, he cramped and almost collapsed in exhaustion.<ref name="two" />

His battle prowess was realized when he then held his own against three [[Battle meditation/Legends|battle meditation]]-invigorated Jedi in combat on Tython; a group which included [[Raskta Lsu]], who was considered to be the greatest contemporary duelist in the Order and Farfala. He almost trampled the half-Bothan, but the other man was empowered enough to evade, even as Lsu Force leapt away from his charge, only to be elbowed later.
