It should be noted, however, that the [[Jedi Weapon Master]] managed to score numerous would-be lethal hits on Bane during this duel, and as such his impenetrable armor was of paramount importance to his victory. Indeed, the Echani woman scissor kicked him from behind and his wrist got clipped with Johan's lightsaber so he lost his weapon for several seconds before his wrist healed and he recalled it. Additionally, his victory came only after the Jedi's battle meditation ceased, and Raskta Lsu was killed by a sneak attack from Zannah. During this duel, Zannah noted that Bane's lightsaber technique was somewhat unrefined, less so than Sarro Xaj to be sure. However, this lack of refinement was intentional, as Bane believed that eschewing technical sophistication for fury-driven, strength-oriented swordplay increased his effectiveness as a duelist, born out by how he almost clove off Farfala's hand and while the Jedi was warned to parry, Bane still knocked the blade away. Soon after, he took Johan's hand and used his arm to smack away Farfala's blade hand, opening the lord up to be decapitated. During combat, Darth Bane was likened by his enemies to a force of nature.<ref name="two" />

In his later years, Darth Bane's speed and skill with such that he was able to deflect torrents of rain with his lightsaber for ten continuous minutes. On Prakith, he mostly used his powers to fight and held back his fury, though he did without slowing use his blade and Force chokes just after he made a death field and killed a man without effort. Likewise, while caught by surprise on his adopted homeland and flashbanged, he was able to kill two men with his saber in between throwing Force attacks to kill many others, though he got laid low by the Huntress landing a blow with a tainted blade. During his breakout from the Stone Prison, he killed several people and evaded his student in a fight, though she had a lightsaber and he did not.  The Huntress foresaw that he could well slay Zannah or be killed by her.<ref name="doe" />

Then on Ambria, for his final battle with Zannah he was forced to unchain his full prowess one last time. He first traded blows and managed to smack Zannah with his body and forehead to an extent, then unleashed new moves and moved faster than his student had ever seen, Trading more blows, the Sith Master was able to pounce on her when she fell over and though she kept his saber-strikes off, she could not stop him from breaking her rib with a kick. He evaded most of the sorceress's dark side tendrils, though one hit him and nearly knocked him out with the horror and pain. Even still with such a horrible wound, he was able to disarm his student and knock her down, and would have impaled her, if not for her magic tentacles cutting off his weapon arm.<ref name="doe" />

When he was no longer afforded the protection of orbalisk armor, Bane adapted a more complex and unpredictable style that incorporated feints and defensive maneuvers.<ref name="doe" /> He was also skilled in [[Form III/Legends|Soresu]], and taught his apprentice Darth Zannah Form III to complement her petite physical frame.<ref name="two" /> Bane was even proficient in [[Form VII/Legends|Juyo]],<ref name="TotG">''[[Threats of the Galaxy]]''</ref> which he used in his final duel with Zannah,<ref name="doe" /> and was an excellent brawler and unarmed combatant, thanks to his time in the mines of Apatros.<ref name="pod" /><ref name="doe" /> At one time, he had displayed superb [[mounted lightsaber combat]] while controlling a drexl and fighting three Beast Riders; he managed to deflect blaster bolts from every single one of his opponents in the sky.<ref name="two" /> Bane was also extremely adept at utilizing the [[Dun Möch/Legends|Dun Möch]] technique, outsmarting and demoralizing his rival, Sirak, in their rematch at the Sith Academy.<ref name="pod" />
===Force powers===
{{Quote|I know many rituals. Many secrets. And I have the strength to use them.|Bane|<ref name="pod" />}}
[[File:BaneRuusan_EGF.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Bane using the power of the Force to create a titanic Force Storm on Ruusan alongside the rest of the Sith elite.]]
Darth Bane was very talented in the Force. As a miner on Apatros, he was able to use the Force on occasion, though he had no understanding of it and his use was largely instinctive. However, after he received formal training at the Korriban Academy, Bane became one of the most skilled students there. He was highly dedicated to his training and spent [[Standard hour/Legends|hours]] reading ancient Sith texts, knowledge that was forsaken by the school's other attendees. In addition, he received private lessons in the ways of the dark side, and excelled. He desired to become a great and powerful Sith Lord, and spent a tremendous amount of time practicing, in hopes of perfecting his skills, surpassing even the last leader of the Sith in Kaan's own estimation.<ref name="pod" /> He went on to found his own Sith Order, ascend to be a greatly powerful Sith<ref name="two" /> personally discovered the hidden lore of at least four legendary Sith Lords from their holocrons, those of Darth Revan,<ref name="pod" /> Freedon Nadd, Belia Darzu,<ref name="two" /> and Darth Andeddu, and became a respected influence to the Sith who came after him.<ref name="doe" />

====Young Man, Dark Potential====
As a young man, Dessel had a limited use and little understanding of the Force. One of the first times he used the dark side was to kill his father by telekinetically destroying his heart through instinct and anger (when this was later made clear to him, he was shaken). He also used a split of foresight to win a fistfight. His life changed when he foresaw that there was a Sabbac switch incoming, which let him know that there was an [[Idiot's Array/Legends|Idiot's Array]] coming up. He won the game, but was accused of cheating. Insulted, Dessel [[Consume Essence|feed on the emotions of]] one man he had beaten, and giddy with this power had fantasies of cracking a world as his rage infected everyone nearby almost into inciting a riot. That night, he sensed when the three troopers he had won money from were coming to attack him and in the brawl, he reflexively through the Force saw a vibro-blade "glowing" to him in the night.<ref name="pod" />

As a soldier, Dessel instinctively used the Force, such that he took it for granted. He was able to [[Force sense/Legends|sense traps]] and [[Life Sense|find enemies]], using this through his army career, especially on Kashyyyk where he saved his squad with this skill. He also used his negative emotions like hate to overcome his fears and up his resolve. On Hsskhor, he [[Precognition/Legends|knew before the battle was over]] that the Sith would loose the battle, so he knew to have his squad fall back. During the Battle of Phaseera, he got the feeling that something major was about to happen, and indeed he would soon become a Sith. In that battle, Dessel was faced with a seemingly impossible situation, that being slaying enough enemies to allow his squad to do a mission before getting torn apart by the defenders' turrets. More than a hundred meters from the site he was ordered to raid, he took Lucia's sniper rifle and sensed where to shoot, then with [[Force speed/Legends|Force-empowered speed]] shot the three turret gunners and then gun down five more men and women in less than as three seconds. Midway through his shooting spree, he was blinded by a flashbang but on reflex used [[Force sight]] to keep aware of where to blast. The soldier also [[Force empathy/Legends|empathically]] felt one of his foe's fear. When he was rescued from prison by a Sith Lord, he felt how powerful the Sith was and the power in a room they spoke in. Lord Kopecz thought that the new student's power was small as of then, but could grow to master status.<ref name="pod" />

====Sith Student====
Bane was a very fast learner, and quickly passed many students at the Korriban Academy in just a few months, getting the masters' attention, seeming to become stronger than another student each week. Qordis said his power was without limit if he embraced the Sith Code. He possessed great telekinetic power, shown early when he Force pushed another Sith and pulled a sword to himself after his arm was disabled in a training duel, and could shatter some opponents' Force shield, as he did with Fohargh when he tapped into his anger to knock him over and then crushed Fohargh's neck. Though, the act broke him morally and he withdrew into himself in doubt, and he became weak in doubt until he returned to the dark. He was demolished by Sirak when the other man fought with the Force and Bane could not really push or block him or fight well without the dark side being embraced. When a Tuk'ata attacked him, he flung it with the Force. He also pulled his saber hilt to himself and slammed a person down when Sirak and two others tried to kill him, but he and his friend took their lives.<ref name="pod" />

Githany went into his mind after his depression and helped him move back to the darkness. She then taught him new Force powers. After just a single hour-long practice session with Githany, Bane exhibited a capacity with Force lightning that surpassed even Sirak (all the other students could only make a few sparks at first), throwing bolts of lightning to blow up shelves of scrolls, a power so strong it was thought they could ruin a room (but he could still look at them while she could not stand to do so) and caused a windstorm charged with electrical energy when he did this the first time.<ref name="pod" />

In matters of perception, he was able to [[Life Detection|sense life around himself]], like the Pelko bugs in a tomb and the [[Receptive Telepathy|surface thoughts of others]]. He also could [[Truth-sense|tell that Githany was not lying to him]] at the academy.  He used an [[Aura of uneasiness|aura of weakness]] to hide his progress from other students, though if a master had wanted to, he could have probably seen through it. He continued to use the Force to sense traps such as in the Korriban tombs, and to sense his foes' like Sirak's fighting style much like how he [[Force empathy/Legends|empathically felt]] Sirak's confusion when Githay joined Bane during the other's ambush to kill him.<ref name="pod" />

Regarding the body, he was able to go into a [[Healing meditation|meditation so as to use dark side healing]], and he almost never needed to [[Sleep/Legends|sleep]] except when pushed to extreme exhaustion. Instead, he relied on an hour or two of daily [[Meditation/Legends|meditation]] to keep his body energized and his mind invigorated use an hour or two of meditation and would sometimes go without food and drink by [[Force Sustenance|using the Force to sustain himself]], a skill he trained as a Sith student and used when he ran out of food during his sabbatical to the Sith tombs along with keeping his [[Remove Fatigue|exhaustion at bay]], though his thirteen days of keeping himself going and fighting some monsters nearly claimed all his power and damaged his body using the Force so much. Of course, when he fought, he used the Force to fight better and unleash saber forms to the point that his mentor praised his skills when he [[Battlemind|used the Force to fight better]]; when he fought Sirak he used a [[Force speed/Legends|surge of speed]] and [[Enhance Attribute|strength]], moving faster than could be seen to hit hard enough to break bones and a training sword.<ref name="pod" />

====Rogue Darth====
On Lehon, Bane used the Force for many tasks, [[Telekinesis/Legends|telekinetically]] pushing a button to open Revan's Holocron container, washing the pyramid with the dark side to turn it on; and when it was worn out and he had learned all he could, crushing it with the Force as the creator would have wanted. When he foguht Ka'seem, he was able to push the other Sith but in turn was Force thrown and had to conjure a Force barrier so that his neck snapped not upon the impact. The Dark Lord's telekinetic prowess was such that when given time to build up an attack due to his enemy pausing to give a speech, he caused the battleground of the Temple of the Ancients on Lehon to collapse with a Force Wave mixed with Force lightning that could have pulped a person, which resulted in the death of Kas'im. However, it was not Bane's attack that directly slew him since the teacher raised a ward of telekinetic blockage, rather the part of the temple that fell which crushed the other man. When he lay dying from Githany's second poison, he still had enough power to lift his lightsaber and then float it around, using kinetic combat to slay two children, just enough feedable agony to get him going to kill the rest of the family alike. He then lifted Caleb's daughter, over a boiling pot and threatened to drop her into it, unless he was healed. On Russan, he was ready to block speeder fire by [[Force barrier/Legends|conjuring a Force shield]] and killed Qordis with a Force choke, tearing through the teacher's own Force barrier.<ref name="pod" /> He was able to [[Force deflection/Legends|turn around Zannah's Force push]] and magnify it to knock her over. When he ambushed a group of his former allies who had deserted, he shot a dozen lines of lightning that cooked two men to death in seconds, conjured a Force wave during that battle that uprooted and shredded tents and wood crates, as well as snapped a woman's neck, then killed a man with a saber throw he gracefully recalled in a moment. Days later on Duxn, he conjured a [[protection bubble]] to keep himself safe (though tossed around and banged up badly) when his ship crashed and slid for a kilometer. Doing so took all his power and he had to build up his energy for the perfect moment. In Nadd's tomb, he moved a magical barrier rock into the Holocron room, though he had to make two tries, the second giving it all he had, though try as he might he could't break it with his power. When he fled the Orbalisks, he was able to move the stone into place much faster to seal them, since he had a new well of painful urgency. While inside, he smacked some of the creatures with a Force strike and held them away with Force deflection and his blade, but still some latched onto him.<ref name="two" />

From Reven's Holocron, he learned much in his weeks of study, more than he had before from the other teachers.<ref name="pod" /> Though he had little skill in sorcery except for a couple of rituals he put special effort into being able to employ,<ref name="doe" /> he duly read of [[Sith sorcery/Legends|spells too hard and complex for him to use]], but that he duly wrote down. Most important of all, he learned of the fearful [[Thought bomb|Thought Bomb]], a ritual he could trigger but would never dare to use, but with which he destroyed Kaan's Brotherhood by tricking Kaan into using it. In collective focus with the other Sith Masters of the Brotherhood, there was one sorcery he dared: Bane led the [[Alter Environment|unleashing of a lightning storm]] that consumed Ruusan's landscape with a flurry of flames and death. This ritual was much like that of the Thought Bomb, where the Sith, in this case taking all the so called Dark Lords working with Bane joined their thoughts with Bane as the focus. The rite caused dark clouds to form, winds to blow, and the sky to be riven by lightning. Bane drew the lightning into himself then, with the new power gave lines of it to the other Sith as he floated five meters upwards. Boasting that now they would kill a world, Bane directed the magic, invoking a rain of hundreds of forks of lighting as his sight glared down from on high. The storm drove the Jedi out of their encampment, but before the Sith could wipe them out, Kaan and the other Sith left the attack, desiring the fun of closer combat and fearing Bane.<ref name="pod" />

Bane continued to augment his body, using the Force to [[Battlemind|guide his attack and defense]] against the great blademaster, then later [[Force jump/Legends|Force jumping]] away from Ka'seem in combat.<ref name="pod" /> He showed he could leap ten meters when he killed some rogue Sith soldiers and getting there he ran with dark side-assisted [[Force speed/Legends|speed]] to get to the battle.<ref name="two" /> Bane used the Force to smell poison on Githany's lips when she kissed him. He was also able to sense poisons in himself and with Revan's teachings could often cure himself by [[Detoxify Poison|purging the toxins from his body]], so long as the poison did not set in before he realized and removed it. Githany's Synox, the true attack venom, was an example of something that did get past his guard, so when he studied himself and tried to [[Pyrokinesis|burn it out with the chill fire of Bogan]], but was then so weak he could only slow the spread.The Sith could also enter a [[Hibernation trance/Legends|hibernation trance]] if he chose to. By [[Consume Essence|channeling the pain and anguish of others to fuel the dark side]], Bane could sustain or invigorate himself. However, Bane was still susceptible to the flaw of Dark Side based [[Force healing/Legends|healing]] requiring the use of inner darkness to maintain, as shown by how while he was able to sustain himself after being poisoned by the Brotherhood of Darkness long enough to be cured by Caleb, though after supping on a battlefield's pain echos and reaching for the ghosts of the death, yet he needed to further kill to tap into the pain of three farmer children and the anguish of the father to accomplish it, which gave him the last few hours he needed to find a cure.<ref name="pod" /> After killing a few people as he was leaving Russan, he again supped on the emotions of the dead. Furthermore, Bane had the theoretical ability to draw upon the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|Light Side of the Force]] to [[Force healing/Legends|heal]] himself, such as to heal his broken arm, but refrained from ever doing so—believing that invoking the Light would be against everything the Sith stood for, as well as ultimately deny him the chance to grow though suffering.<ref name="two" /> 

After declaring himself to be a Darth, Bane stole a ship and flew it to Lehon, using the Force to fly well for an hour past the debris around the world. Bane sensed a Rancor on his way to the temple, so he [[Animal bond|took control over it]] with great strain and also [[Drain Knowledge|rooted around its memories]] to learn about the place he was. His [[Sense Force|sense/see Force capacity let him perceive]] Temple of the Elders as the loadstone of the Force it was. Bane did a [[Force sense/Legends|mental scan]] of the land near the temple to make sure his blade teacher had come alone to face him, just before their deadly duel. After he fell in exhaustion and Ka'seem in stone and death, he used his Force sense to seek life underneath the rubble and found nothing. When poisoned, he used his Force powers to guide him where to drive and his ''prima vitae'' picked up some scavengers. When he came to Russan, he sensed the world's Force status as a grey mess, both sides of the Force having been unleashed so and the two sides also tainted by each others' ideology. Likewise, on the planet he was able to get a vague sense of where the Jedi were, but could not crack their Force Stealth.<ref name="pod" /> He sensed when Zannah was drawing on the Force to trip him, but his Force sense failed to pick up Zannah approaching him a fact he wondered if owed to distraction or her hiding her presence, though before felt the emotions of both Zannah, her spite towards the Jedi since her cousins were lost and when the Sith army deserters were scared of his murderous assault. On the tombworld of Nadd, he was able to sense for hundreds of kilometers that there were trees and that the tomb was a few kilometers away. After the Thought Bomb, he [[Precognition/Legends|sensed the danger posed by eight people and learned their backgrounds and genders from two kilometers]]. However, on Duxon, he only precoged a big cat attacking him when it was too late and would have perished if not for it getting confused. He [[Force sight|saw what he needed to in the Force]] when he went to kill the eight Sith army deserters.<ref name="two" />

He shivered when the Thought Bomb's blast wave hit him, but still reached his Force sense out again and found that every member of the Brotherhood was dead. In addition, Bane had a [[Force-bond/Legends|Force-bond]] with Githany (and so she received [[Force vision/Legends|visions]] of him). Upon finding a girl called Rain, [[Sense Force Potential|he determined she was strong in the Force]],<ref name="pod" /> and by this same art that Tomcat was poor in the Force, barely able to use it.<ref name="two" /> Bane was able to easily resist Skere Kaan's [[Mind trick/Legends|mind tricks]], while the other Dark Lords in the Brotherhood were unable to do so. For his part, Bane also could compel people with the Force.<ref name="pod" /> However, he was still in agony when the Thought Bomb washed over him, leaving his brain in pain for days and it was a strain to touch the Thought Bomb, but endured the fire and ice-like agony its surface was, though he kept his mind safe from the thoughts of the dead, which tore them up even more. On his route to Nadd's tomb, he seemed haunted by Quordis's ghost, until he blasted out dark side power to dispel the ghost, though this broke the controls of his ship. He was forced to [[Mechu-deru|use the dark side to control the engines]], his first effort only earning him a shower of sparks, but the second attempt working just well enough.<ref name="two" />

====In Orbalisks Clad====
Darth Bane began to test his new powers almost as soon as he became bitten by the creatures at Nadd's tomb. He used the Force to study the bugs and felt physically faster and more perceptive, his healing the greater by the parisites, and more connected to the power of the Force and also balanced with the risk of losing control of his powers. By the time he was parted from his suit, he said his sheer amount of power made it easy for Jedi to sense him. He also used a pulse of the dark side to awaken Nadd's holocron. With this new power from the Orbalisks, he made a Force burst to rid himself of the seeming ghosts of Kaan and Qordis who had haunted him. When he was ambushed on Ambria in 990 BBY, the Sith assassins were able to [[Dim Other's Senses|dull his perceptions]], but he noticed just in time and with a [[Force suppression|burst of red light, dispelled their arts]] and illusions of hiding. He also burst Farfala's stasis field after less than a second. After he got hold of Belia Darzu's holocron and slew her monster guards, he rested, then when ready used his will to turn it on and flip through it, seeking knowledge.<ref name="two" />

After getting the orbalisks bonded to him, one of Bane's first acts was to fly on a drexl from Duxon to Onderon, keeping himself and his mount safe from the near lack of atmosphere by making a [[Protection bubble|protective bubble]] around them. Soon after arriving, he intervened to save his apprentice from slavers, telekinetically tearing the saddle off a drexl and sending the crew falling to their deaths so fast he could not sup on their suffering. At the end of the battle, exerting all the power he could muster and the might he reaved by employing both consume essence and drawing upon the parisites on his body for more power, he erected a Force barrier that let him just survive a crash of three of the flying beasts that excavated a 2 meter deep and twenty wide crater, though this spent all his Force energy and most of his physical stamina. He several times had to made thousands of subatomic alterations to the items he wanted to turn into holocrons over hundreds of hours. When his fourth holocron failed, in a fit of rage he mind-flung fuel canisters fifty meters to express his anger. When a group of Shadow Assassins came at him, during the fight he make a wide attack with the Force, knocking over two, hurling a pair away, leaving only one who was able to withstand the push before Bane used his saber to slay this last one; then he flung a push at Zannah that would have broken her bones if she had not blocked it, toning its impact down to just pushing her away. On Tython, he pushed down a door after charging up his might, then soon had to use similar skills on technobeasts, at one point breaking twelve with the Force, later disintegrating two more with his powers. When the Jedi came to abolish the Sith on Tython, Bane hit Raskta Lsu with a Force wave, which would have killed the Echani woman if not for Farfala throwing a Force shield around her.<ref name="two" />

In his years clad in the parisites, he continued to use lightning as well as telekinesis, burning a trio of marauders to ash and killing their winged beast with a bolt during his fight to keep Zannah from the drexl-riders. During one of his spouts of rage at failing to make a holocron, Zannah found him amid lightning-burned ground after he had burned his clothes off and made the air thick with static, so furious were his blasts of lightning. When Hetton attacked him, for once his lightning powers were cheated, when the other darksider made a Force-empowered leap away from his spray of a dozen stands. On Tython he made a wave of lightning ripple out and destroy a dozen techobeasts, much like he pulsed blue electricity when he was disarmed by the Jedi on Tython. Moments before, he shot a bolt at Farfala, blowing through the other man's Force wall, only for Lsu to save her fellow Jedi Master with her sabers.<ref name="two" /> At some point in the battle, he sent lightning at Sarro Xaj, only for the other human to block it on his saber, the tiny tendrils that got past seeming to do little harm.<ref>''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> His powers almost were his undoing, when he conjured a massive lightning bolt to finish off Othone, only for Worror to use his last moments of life to cage the dark power. Bane's lightning flashed around the blue shell, his azure assault bouncing around and glowing too bright to look at as he burned off his own robe and melting his specialized gear, and killed many of the animals that made his armor. Bane was thus left on the edge of death only able to live with his own endurance, his orblisks at last overtaxed.<ref name="two" />

His powers of the mind continued to be potent, using the power of Beast trick to tame a drexel on Duxon and succeeding on his second attempt though it attacked him after the first, then so gaining total control over the creature. He, as before, showed the capacity to know the future, such as when he foresaw that Zannah was going to make it to Onderon (so he was able to rescue her from some slavers). On Tython, he sensed the dark side aura of Belia Darzu's fortress and that he should go to that and later he sensed Zannah and Daraovit were aboard a ship and that the other man was a weak user of the Force, but did have the Force. Much like this, he sensed the power and light of the Jedi who were coming on Zannah's heels to slay the Sith.<ref name="two" />

Though he admitted he was a poor sorcerer, leaving the idea of Sith magic for Zannah after he tested her, he did attempt to create his own holocon. Besides the thousands of microscopic alterations by telekinesis he did to whenever he tried to make his own item of knowledge, he twice tried to make one with Sith sorcery glyphs but failed over the course of some months, the first time even imploding into a flash of white light. Eight years after he claimed the rank of leader of the Sith, he learned the symbols needed to be personal but on his third effort took two weeks, too long. Bane crushed the failure in his bare hands.  Another, he attempted to make two years later, but once more failed and after three days and nights, was so tired he lost control to the parisites and his powers blew up the item by mistake. He also resolved to study Belia Darzu's teachings on Force alchemy.<ref name="two" />

His physical prowess and combat skill was guided by the dark side to kill the last four of the Shadow Assassins who were led to him as part of Zannah's plan to get him a holocon template, then went into a Force rage when he thought Zannah had turned on him and after killing the newcomers, sunk deeper into anger and nearly slew her in his furious attack. During this fight he leapt at his student, his jump boosted by the Force, a move he also used to get next to and kill Worror. On Tython, he could have called on Bogan to destroy the technobeast virus (though the chemicals in his parasites worked to protect him so well he did not need to) and used the dark side to [[Remove Fatigue|reduce his tiredness]]. When his lightning barrage got caged in with him he lived for four days with his power in the Force before a proper healer could be coerced to help him. When he tried to get Zannah to kill him on Ambria, his eyes glowed with his dark power with the intensity of his demands.<ref name="two" />

====Dark Lord====
By 990 BBY, Bane had amassed an enormous amount of strength in the Force, viewing his power as nearly infinite and well above needing to bother with using props like Sith amulets. When he tapped into the dark side power that suffused Andeddu's Keep on Prakith, Darth Bane projected a [[Force drain/Legends|death field]] that darkened the air around him and instantaneously desiccated and killed the attacking Malevolence cultists who had been unable to avoid it, aging their bodies a thousand years in a moment. This technique was extremely taxing however, and would have rapidly exhausted Bane if hadn't replenished it by feeding on the dark side, draining energies from those caught in it. While the Huntress was able to bring him down with a poisoned sword, during his resultant captivity, once Lucia gave him a cure for the poison in him, he used his powers of flame to burn out most of the lingering bad effects and now that he had been subjected and so forcibly educated in it, Bane could also destroy Senflax.<ref name="doe" />

By 990 BBY, Bane was able to cast electric voltage so strong that most opponents died instantly upon contact, the energy output leaving their bodies burned and charred.<ref name="doe" />

On Prakith, he killed several dark side cultists with Force chokes as he advanced. He was able to plunge deep into his hate and draw fully on the power of the dark side to unleash powerful Force waves, the strength of which devastated almost anything in their path.<ref name="doe" /> 

Bane owned and had access to a vast collection of Sith scrolls, tomes, and texts. With the help of individuals like Argel Tenn, he was able to obtain ancient Sith manuscripts and artifacts.<ref name="doe" /> He got the the instructions for the creation of a holocron of his own. The Sith sorcery he learned from Nadd's holocron was admittedly beyond the scope of Bane's abilities,<ref name="two" /> although the stolen ritual of essence transfer from Andeddu's device was well within. Bane's own construction, created some point before 980 BBY, was a small, pyramid-shaped device that contained all of his knowledge, which he planned to pass down to future Dark Lords in his Sith Order. The gatekeeper for Bane's holocron was his own orbalisk-clad likeness.<ref name="doe" /> His initial attempts to create a holocron ended in failure, which Bane came to believe was due to his orbalisk armor; it provided him with great power in battle, but he believed that it robbed him of the ability to use his powers for more subtle tasks. He eventually discovered that he was simply skipping a critical step in the holocron's creation out of ignorance, and later rectified his mistake.<ref name="two" /> Another dark trick he had was i[[Taint|mprinting his presence on a place]], so that someone hunting him with the Force would sense that spot instead of his true location.<ref name="doe" />

He was deeply attuned to the currents of light and dark, when great secrets could be teased out of the galaxy and he could sometimes thusly divine the will of the Force. The Dark Lord was able to Force sense a rainfall, detecting every drop and using the Force to improve his Form Three talents so that he could dodge and parry all the storm for ten minutes.<ref name="doe" />

Bane could keep on calling on the dark side to empower his body.  On Prakith, he employed the art of enhance attribute to gain the strength to manually rip a metal hatch off.<ref name="doe" />

At some point, he saw a vision of Coruscant under Sith rule, something that would not come to be for hundreds of years.<ref name="BoS" /> He was deeply attuned to the currents of light and dark, when great secrets could be teased out of the galaxy and he could sometimes thusly divine the will of the Force. His Force sense was keen enough to sense every drop in a deluge while he used the Force to augment his skill in Form Three to hold off the rainfall for ten minutes.  His ''prima vitae'' revealed to him where the Malevolence cultists were scurrying around him in their fortress on Prakith, there being nearly a hundred. He also sensed the power of the dark side clerics and knew that none of them could withstand him alone, but if they fought together, they might be able to defeat him.<ref name="doe" />

Bane was highly resistant to poison, and escaped death by its means on several occasions.<ref name="pod" /> Serra noted while torturing him that the drugs had surprisingly little impact on him.<ref name="doe" />

He also possessed remarkable willpower and determination. He was able to force Andeddu's holocron to reveal to him knowledge that the holocron's gatekeeper was actively attempting to keep from him, and was skilled enough to attempt the deadly ritual of essence transfer.<ref name="doe" />

===Other skills===
As Dessel, he was a canny gambler and used insults to prod people to make bad game choices. The future Dark Lord was able to read his opponents and conceal his own feelings, talents which he used to become a talented sabacc player. Bane was a master of deception, and used his skills to fool others even before he received formal training. When he became a Sith army footsoldier, he survived at least a dozen battles in a year and became a sergeant. As a Sith trooper, he took the lives of hundreds or thousands of Republic soldiers. Early in his Sith training, he leapt up ten meters and could run five kilometers. Sometimes he could refuse to fall to insults. Bane was able to convince Githany to join him against Sirak, though he failed to bring her over to his Rule of Two ideology. Bane had scientific knowledge, enough to know the difference between male and female Rancors. He could give massages to help people feel better. Though, he endured a life of hard mining, being a soldier, Sith study and privation, and even keep driving through his poisoning to butcher his way to a cure. On Russan, he kicked another Sith's skull in, ending the mortally wounded man's life. He could put on an act like the best [[Actor/Legends|dramatist]] of [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]] which let him make Kaan think the leader had subdued him with his mental influence.<ref name="pod" />

Bane could break a Neek's neck with ease and displayed a great tolerance for physical pain, such as that brought on by the orbalisk armor he was forced to wear. After being wounded almost unto death by his own rebounded lightning storm, he barely held on for four days before healing, then he was too weak to use the Force or to do more than say two words and slept for two more. When imploring Zannah to kill him, he was able to sit up. On her ship, he grappled her and could have crushed her neck, until she explained she was a proper Sith and had deceived the Jedi. Still, it was said that he would have to rest for weeks or months before he could move properly.<ref name="two" />

The Dark Lord was able to use the infestation to his benefit by taking the pain and fueling his dark side rage with it. Besides being impenetrable to lightsabers, the orbalisks also provided Bane with chemical enhancements to his senses, stamina, strength, and speed. In the armor, he got back up after a drexl knocked him over, withstood force pike charges that together could have laid low a bantha, and lived through being smacked by a rancor. Furthermore, it provided him with an enhanced healing factor; a knife wound that Bane once inflicted upon himself, for instance, healed virtually as he made it, the Technobeast virus had not chance against the black bugs chemicals in Bane, and even a debilitating lightsaber strike to his arm from Johun Othone healed within seconds. Most importantly, Bane could tap into the parasites' ability to draw on the dark side to greatly increase his own power while they remained attached to him. One drawback to being infested with the orbalisks was that, because they drew on Bane's power to feed themselves, he was only capable of performing delicate tasks with the Force for a somewhat limited period of time. This was due to the fact that, in order to precisely modulate his powers for subtle tasks, he had to cut the orbalisks completely off from the dark side. This in turn caused the parasites to pump increasingly greater amounts of mood-altering chemicals into Bane's body in an attempt to get him to draw more strongly on the dark side, and thus feed them. Bane was capable of resisting the effects of the chemicals, including ever-mounting levels of pain, for a significant period of time. However, he was not immune to them, and at one point considered ridding himself of the parasites due to this problem. Ultimately, he discovered that the orbalisks did not cause nearly as great an issue with his abilities as he had feared and resolved to keep them.<ref name="two" />

In his last days, Bane sometimes felt a clash between his physical might such as how he kicked the covers off his bed, left a clear dent when he hit a table, and trained strenuously; and his age, exacerbated and prematurely deepened by the suit he had worn and the constant dark energies his pulled through his body and meditated upon. His frequent hand tremor was just the most obvious of the physical ailments he had, an issue he could not cure. He was rendered slower and weaker at rest or practice than he had been, to the point that his muscles groaned and joints clicked when he did Form V lightsaber training. He even considered just going back to bed once instead of training in the rain, but the Sith pushed on and completed the set. On Prakith, he was able to wrench a tomb cover open and yank out Andeddu's holocron. In addition to his athletic skills, he was a skilled pilot who made hundreds of hyperspace jumps as he sought for Darth Andeddu's holocron and landed his ship safely. The Sith was not invulnerable, of course, being staggered and stunned by a sonic attack during the raid on his house on Ciutric IV and during the furious battle, though he unleashed his powers--even punching through his powers being partly suppressed--he got blinded and pushed back by flash gernades and kicked over a banister. Though he recovered his dropped saber and slashed down two men, the Huntress was able to cut him with her sword and as he dodged blaster bolts and chased the other Force user, he passed out from the poison hidden on the Iktotchi woman's weapon. When Serra tortured him, he went through ten seconds and then almost twice that in poison seizures that made him dreary and almost unable to talk. With a bit of help, he was able to recover and use his powers to shatter his chains with his will and then break out, killing two men with his hands, knifing a woman, and gunning down two more guards whose shots he dodged. After all this effort, he still was able to bodyslam his way though a door. In his last battle, his unarmed strikes broke Zannah's bones and he kept on fighting even after a dark side tendril struck off part of his shoulder and filled him with the dread of absolute annihilation, the cold horror of the void itself.<ref name="doe" />

Underpinning his deeds was a deep intelligence. Bane determined that a newway of Sith practice, his Rule of Two, needed to be exalted to replace the Brotherhood of Darkness.<ref name="pod" /> He was a very skilled teacher in the dark side, using insults and yelling along with philosophy and encouragement to train Zannah to become a Sith. He also was a crafty planner, he made sure to make dossiers on the various Jedi who might be a threat to him and exploited their lack of central authority and control to slip Zannah into the Jedi Temple, pretending to be a random Jedi Padawan. By the time of his near death at his own hand, he had a hundred political plans set in motion. The Sith noticed at a glance that Hetton was not learned in the use of his green lightsaber and Bane was trained in first aid.<ref name="two" /> Considered by his student to be a master manipulator, he set up a bunch of political plots up, such as his informants in the Desilijic Hutt clan and some of his investments repaid themselves a hundred times over. Bane also developed more self-control in the decade after he was forced to shed his armor, his agressive instinct where he might have blindly charged in was tempered by the time he went after Andeddu's pyramid of knowledge. He also made sure to learn the name and reputation of every Jedi Master. A canny debater, he almost got Serra to agree that he was in the right, even as she was torturing him for killing her father. Almost a thousand years after he fell, the path he saw and set Zannah on would bear fruit,<ref name="doe" /> with the Jedi being smashed and a Sith Lord rising to rule the galaxy as Emperor.<ref name="rots" />

Darth Bane was an [[Author/Legends|author]], writing about Sith ideology and training in his essay ''The Rule of Two'', a seminal work that Palpatine included in his own textbook on the dark side. Though, in this, Bane did make<ref name="BoS" /> a slight error in the genetic relation between his student and her kinsman.<ref name="two" /><ref name="BoS" />

==Equipment==
[[File:Valcyn.jpg|thumb|left|200px|The ''Valcyn'']]
During his time in the Gloom Walkers unit, Dessel used a [[TC-22 blaster rifle]]. He became skilled in the use of the weapon, and chose to stick with the first blaster he learned to use instead of switching to a different weapon. As a sergeant, Dessel was allowed to wield a secondary weapon, and so carried an advanced [[GSI-21D|GSI-21D pistol]], able to [[Disintegrator|disintegrate]] armor. He also kept a [[Vibroblade/Legends|vibroblade]] in his [[Boot/Legends|boot]]. Upon entry into the Sith Academy, Bane was trained in lightsaber combat with [[Durasteel/Legends|durasteel]] [[Training lightsaber/Legends|training sabers]] that were covered in the poisonous barbs of the [[pelko bug]]. Later, his blade mentor presented him with a hook-handle lightsaber, that would remain his sword. On Russan, he wore the Sith armor his people were expected to be clad in.<ref name="pod" />

For a time, Bane flew the starship ''Valcyn'', a [[T-class long-range personal cruiser/Legends|''T''-class long-range personal cruiser]] that had originally belonged to Qordis. After he returned from the tombs on Korriban in an effort to find knowledge, Bane declared his abandonment of the Brotherhood, and aware that Qordis would not try to stop him, left the planet in the Headmaster's ship. Bane traveled to Lehon, Ambria, and Ruusan in the highly advanced ship before he crashed on Dxun.<ref name="pod" /><ref name="two" /> By 980 BBY, the Dark Lord had come to own a ''Theta''-class T-1 vessel named the ''Triumph''. The Cygnus Spaceworks vessel could be flown by one [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]], which Bane used to his advantage in 980 BBY when he made a trip to the Deep Core planet Prakith without informing his apprentice. His return trip to his mansion on Ciutric IV proved to be Bane's final journey in his shuttle, as he was ambushed on the planet and taken to Doan.<ref name="doe" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Character origins===
{{Quote|One of the themes throughout the films is that the Sith lords, when they started out thousands of years ago, embraced the dark side. They were greedy and self-centered and they all wanted to take over, so they killed each other. Eventually, there was only one left, and that one took on an apprentice. And for thousands of years, the master would teach the apprentice, the master would die, the apprentice would then teach another apprentice, become the master, and so on. But there could never be any more than two of them, because if there were, they would try to get rid of the leader, which is exactly what Vader was trying to do, and that's exactly what the Emperor was trying to do. The Emperor was trying to get rid of Vader, and Vader was trying to get rid of the Emperor.|George Lucas|<ref Name="Time">{{BookCite|author=Moyers, Bill; Lucas, George|container=Of Myth And Men|title=[[Wikipedia:Time (magazine)|TIME]]|date=1999-04-18|link=https://web.archive.org/web/20240412102322/https://content.time.com/time/magazine/article/0%2C9171%2C23298-4%2C00.html}}</ref>}}
The character of Darth Bane, and his Rule of Two, were created by [[George Lucas]] as part of his backstory of the Sith he developed for the [[prequel trilogy]].<ref name="Endnotes for the NEC">{{SWArchive|url=eu/lit/ref/f20051025/index.html?page=2|text=Endnotes for ''The New Essential Chronology'' Part One: Tales of the Ancient Republic}}</ref> Bane was first mentioned in [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|''The Phantom Menace'' novelization]] as the creator of the Rule of Two. In 2000, [[The Essential Chronology (real-world book)|''The Essential Chronology'']] [[New Sith Wars#Behind the scenes|collated these events]] with the Battle of Ruusan mentioned in ''[[Dark Forces: Jedi Knight]]'', creating a backstory further developed in [[Star Wars: Jedi vs. Sith|''Jedi vs Sith'']] by [[Darko Macan]] and ''[[Bane of the Sith]]'' by [[Kevin J. Anderson]]. ''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]'' and ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' provided more details, and the latter attempted to correct inconsistencies between ''Jedi vs Sith'' and ''Bane of the Sith''.

In [[2006]], ''[[Darth Bane: Path of Destruction]]'', written by [[Drew Karpyshyn]] was released. Several of the details in it [[Retroactive continuity|contradicted]] previous information about Bane. Another novel about Darth Bane, ''[[Darth Bane: Rule of Two]]'', was released in [[2007]] and fixed some of the conflicting elements. Part of the novel covers ''Bane of the Sith'', while it also invents new history for Bane and his apprentice. A third novel, ''[[Darth Bane: Dynasty of Evil]]'', was released in [[2009]]. Each of these novels expanded on Bane's backstory, with ''Dynasty of Evil'' killing off the Dark Lord.

Many fans were initially confused as to whether Bane or Zannah won the final duel between the two at the end of ''Dynasty of Evil''. Author Drew Karpshyn confirmed a few days later that Zannah had won the duel, although a small remnant of Bane remained in her.<ref name="dkw" />

For the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' television series, Bane was to originally appear, alongside Darth Revan, in the [[The Clone Wars: Season Three|third season]] episode "[[Ghosts of Mortis]]" as an influence to the Force-wielding [[Son/Legends|Son]], an embodiment of the dark side of the Force. Although George Lucas commissioned the scene about two ancient Sith, he later cut it before the scene could be fully animated, since it conflicted with Lucas's views on the Force. Supervising Director [[Dave Filoni]] voiced similar concerns to the inclusion of the two Sith Lords; though the scene would have been appreciated by Expanded Universe fans, he stated that cutting the scene had been the right thing to do.<ref name="Ghosts of Mortis Commentary">{{SW|url=video/ghosts-of-mortis-episode-featurette|text="Ghosts of Mortis" Episode Featurette}}</ref> The fact that Revan later converted to the light side could also have raised continuity issues if he did appear as a Sith spirit.<ref name="KoTOR">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''</ref> Darth Bane himself later appeared in the [[The Clone Wars: The Lost Missions|sixth season]] episode "[[Sacrifice (episode)|Sacrifice]]" as an illusion that Yoda had to face. He was given a previously unseen design and voiced in the episode by [[Mark Hamill]], the actor who played [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] in the original trilogy.<ref name="Sacrifice trivia">{{SW|url=explore/the-clone-wars/ep613|text="Sacrifice" - ''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide|nolive=1}}</ref>

[[Lucasfilm]] official [[Leland Chee]] stated in his blog that Bane's name is based on the word "''Bane'',"<ref name="blog">{{Blog|holocron|28|Darth Names and the Darth Who winner revealed.}}</ref> which means, among other things, "a person or thing that ruins or spoils."<ref name="Bane">{{WebCite|url=https://www.dictionary.com/browse/bane|text=Bane|work=[[Wikipedia:Dictionary.com|Dictionary.com]]|archivedate=20250829104058}}</ref> Jan Duursema's depiction of Bane in ''[[Star Wars: Legacy]]'' was based on the partially completed costume of a fan, [[Thomas J. Spanos]].<ref name="TFN post">{{JCFCite|url=posts/30459895|board=Authors and Artists|thread=The Official Jan Duursema Discussion Thread|user=[[Jan Duursema|Jan_Duursema]]|date=2009-09-29|time=6:22 AM|archivedate=20160521115027}}</ref>

===Contradictions===
[[File:Minifig_bane.jpg|thumb|right|Star Wars Miniatures figure of Darth Bane]]
Various contradictions, both major and minor, exist between sources involving Bane. In both the short story ''Bane of the Sith'' and Bane's biography in ''The New Essential Guide to Characters'', it is implied that Bane trained exclusively beneath Qordis, while in the novel he trained under Qordis and many other Sith Masters.<ref name="pod" /> Also, in ''Bane of the Sith'' and ''Path of Destruction'', Bane's lightsaber hilt is clearly described as being "[[Curved-hilt lightsaber/Legends|hooked]]." However, in almost every illustration, even those from after the publishing of ''Path of Destruction'', Darth Bane is depicted with a standard-hilt lightsaber. The illustrations also frequently depict Bane wielding a purple lightsaber, though this was later corrected on the cover art of ''[[Darth Bane: Rule of Two]]''. A picture of the curved hilt was finally included in ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''.

In ''Bane of the Sith'', Bane escapes from Ruusan when his warning to Kaan not to use the thought bomb goes unheeded. The dark side spirits call him a coward for running, and Bane defends himself by saying that the Sith must survive. Until he gets to Onderon, he intends to resurrect the system of the Brotherhood.<ref name="Bane of the Sith">{{GamerCite|3|Bane of the Sith}}</ref> In ''Path of Destruction'', Bane comes to detest the Brotherhood after studying Revan's holocron and the ancient records when he realizes that the Sith can never be united or equal. He plots to destroy the Brotherhood by giving Kaan the formula for using the thought bomb and feigning to join them under the guise of wanting to take over leadership.<ref name="pod" />

The events of ''Bane of the Sith'' are retold in ''Rule of Two''. In ''Bane of the Sith'', ghosts of Kaan and Qordis appear and Bane learns that the creatures that cover him are called "orbalisks" from Qordis,<ref name="Bane of the Sith" /> but ''Rule of Two'' [[Retroactive continuity|retconned]] the ghosts of Kaan and Qordis into hallucinations resulting from the thought bomb damaging Bane's brain and has Bane learn about the orbalisks from Freedon Nadd's holocron.<ref name="two" />

This article tends to support the details described by ''Path of Destruction'' and ''Rule of Two'', as those are the newer sources and are followed by a sequel. 

Chronologically speaking, [[Darth Rivan]] predates Darth Bane,<ref name="pena" /> and Darth Bane is the author of the Rule of Two.<ref name="pod" /> However, one of the traps in Darth Rivan's fortress, as shown in ''[[A Mon Alone]]'', is based on the Sith adherence to the Rule of Two.<ref name="AMA">{{LivingForce|A Mon Alone}}</ref>

Despite a model for Bane that was created for ''The Clone Wars'' season three episode "[[Ghosts of Mortis]]" that was consistent with his previous appearances, including his orbalisk armor, the season six episode "[[Sacrifice (episode)|Sacrifice]]" features an apparition of Darth Bane that is much different from any of his previous appearances, wearing a suit of armor much different than any of those he had previously been seen wearing.
